title: Ticket #3444: inconsistent priv states when running condor tools
description: this is not a security vulnerability. in the off chance that you are running various condor tools as root, there is a small but important discrepancy. running with the "-debug" flag causes the tool to engage in priv-switching, and so it ends up running as the "condor" user unless the code explicitly switches to root_priv (for example, to fetch a credential). running the same tool without "-debug" means the tool will run with root priv for its entire lifetime. this means running with/without "-debug" can alter the behavior of the tool, which is annoying to say the least. (i noticed this when i had incorrectly set permissions on a certificate file that condor should have been able to read, but in fact was readable only by root) i propose we should always initialize the priv switching code. this mimics the behavior of the condor daemons, which i argue is the desired behavior when an admin is trying to test various things via the command line.
creator: zmiller

title: Ticket #289: my_full_hostname() and Daemon::fullHostname() disagree on hostnames.
description: From the looks of it, my_full_hostname() and Daemon::fullHostname() disagree on hostnames in some cases. It seems like they could share more code than they do, which would ensure that if they are getting the wrong host name, at least they can agree on the wrong name. Still, it is not clear to me that this is a Condor problem, or an incorrectly configured DNS problem. This only seems to be happening on Windows machines, so there may be some local configuration problems as well (i.e. a hosts files is searched first for some reason, etc.)
remarks: 2009-Mar-02 10:51:01 by burnett: From #288: It seems that this may be a DNS problem (or how we seem to break whilst using it): 02/27 23:14:02 Looking for matching Collector on 'nmi-0226.batlab.cs.wisc.edu'... 02/27 23:14:02 Found 'nmi-0226.cs.wisc.edu:0' Somehow, in this instance, on Windows, the master decides it is called nmi-0226.batlab.cs.wisc.edu but when it goes looking for a collector by the same name, the only one it finds is nmi-0226.cs.wisc.edu. You'll of course note the missing batman reference in the second host name. 2009-Oct-08 18:02:21 by danb: my_full_hostname() and Daemon::fullHostname() start with different information, so they can end up with different results if reverse-DNS info is misconfigured or the machine hostname is misconfigured. my_full_hostname() tries to get the canonical hostname for the current machine. Daemon::fullHostname() tries to get the canonical hostname for the IP address associated with the desired daemon. In the case where we are getting the hostname of the collector, this usually involves looking up supplied hostname --> IP --> hostname. I'm going to resolve this ticket, because I don't see that we have a case here of two different ways of doing the same thing and getting two different answers. If we get a specific case in the future where this same problem seems to be happening, we should try to determine whether there is a way for Condor to detect the misconfiguration. 2009-Oct-08 21:30:10 by burnett: On Windows, if your hosts file disagree with the DNS server, then the two functions will return different values. 2009-Oct-08 21:30:56 by burnett: Never-mind, that it what you said.

Ticket #6579: DAGMan does not check for .nodes.log integrity
description: DAGMan uses a log file, *.dag.nodes.log, to coordinate events with the schedd during the execution of a DAG. Every event cycle, DAGMan checks if the log file has grown. If so, it processes any new events that were added; if not, it carries on as if nothing has changed. DAGMan uses the ReadMultipleUserLogs::detectLogGrowth() function to detect log growth. This function returns a boolean value, true or false. If the log file has shrunk, it returns false. If the log file has been erased, it returns false. So if the log file gets corrupted (ie. overwritten by the user), DAGMan just carries on and spins endlessly. We need to change this function to detectLogStatus() or something similar, and return a ReadUserLog::FileStatus object instead. Then DAGMan should look for all varieties of statuses (growth, no change, shrunk, error) and handle them accordingly. In error situations, we should terminate the DAG immediately with a relevant error message.

title: Ticket #1316: Dyanamic Slot INVALIDATE_STARTD_ADS causes collector pegging
description: Dynamic slots will send an INVALIDATE_STARTD_ADS to the collector when they complete a job in order to free up the slot. The problem is that the collector does an O(n) match on the slot query ad. When dynamic slots are coming and going in a large pool with thousands of nodes this can be a serious issue and peg the collector.
remarks: 2010-Mar-30 15:51:03 by danb: I took a look at the patch. Comments: The call to sscanf should specify maximum field widths for the output buffers. The sscanf pattern that is specified for MyAddress will match up to the ':' in the address and then fail to match after that. The part before the colon happens to be all that is required in the hash key. The fact that there is dangling stuff in the query string that is ignored means that in the future if any queries are sent that contain more clauses, those clauses would be ignored. I think we should require an exact match of the query string to the expected format--no trailing junk allowed. The final problem is caused by a somewhat ugly hack in condor. (Even worse, I am the poor soul who pressed the buttons to commit the patch.) When ads are sent to the collector, the value of MyAddress may be rewritten. The IP address is replaced by the IP address of the socket that is being used to talk to the collector. The intention is to make condor advertise the IP address that is most likely to be accessible to others in the pool. When flocking to multiple collectors, it may even choose a different IP address to advertise when talking to the different collectors. How does that cause a problem for this patch? You are sending the address as part of the query. This will not automatically be rewritten. If you put the address in an attribute named MyAddress, then it would be rewritten. I haven't looked in detail at how the query classad is used, but it is possible that you could put the address in MyAddress and refer to it as MyAddress in your query. If that works, then you could do the same sort of thing for Name. Then verifying that the query matches the expected one would be a simple string compare--no pattern matching required. 2010-Mar-30 16:33:46 by tstclair: I agree with the recommendation, and I was planning on it too ;-). That is interesting to note that the MyAddress field changes on subsequent sends , so all the more reason to make the change. (that is going in the mental rolodex) 2010-Mar-31 11:13:30 by danb: I like the new patch! One nitpick: you unwittingly followed the example in Resource::final_update() of how to insert stuff into an ad by using ClassAd::Insert(). That's the old way from days of yore when string constants usually probably never contained special characters that needed to be escaped, and (though clearly not a problem in your code) static buffers were usually probably always big enough for whatever expression was being put in them. It is better to use ClassAd::Assign() or ClassAd::AssignExpr(). Example: line.sprintf( "( TARGET.%s == \"%s\" )", ATTR_NAME, r_name ); invalidate_ad.AssignExpr( ATTR_REQUIREMENTS, line.Value() ); invalidate_ad.Assign( ATTR_NAME, r_name ); invalidate_ad.Assign( ATTR_MY_ADDRESS, daemonCore->publicNetworkIpAddr()); Of course, the above code is still not quite correct because it doesn't worry about escaping r_name in the requirements expression. I bet it just happens that quotes are forbidden in the name, so there probably isn't an actual problem. But nevertheless, it is nice to have the correctness of code easily verifiable. I'll leave it up to you to decide whether it is worth it in this case. One way to do it is this: MyString escaped_name; ClassAd::EscapeStringValue( r_name, escaped_name ); line.sprintf( "( TARGET.%s == \"%s\" )", ATTR_NAME, escaped_name.Value() ); You would not pass escaped_name as the 2nd argument to Assign(), because Assign() does the escaping for you. 2010-Apr-01 08:09:18 by tstclair: Dan - could you please ref the ticket #'s for the afore mentioned MyAddress translation. 2010-Apr-01 09:31:21 by danb: The MyAddress rewriting predates gittrack by a few years. See usage of the function ConvertDefaultIPToSocketIP() in the source code. 2010-Sep-07 12:41:44 by danb: It turns out that it is problematic to have a Name attribute in the invalidation query ad and to refer to Name without specifying TARGET scope in the query requirements. This causes the query to match all ads! If the invalidation query were to ever make its way to a 7.4 collector or to a collector that doesn't have an ad with a matching hash key, then the query is evaluated and all machine ads get invalidated. I've opened a new ticket (#1644) for this issue.

title: Ticket #6129: Create mpich3 (hydra) scripts compatible with parallel universe
description: Open MPI and MPICH2-compatible scripts were updated in #6024. MPICH3 uses the Hydra launcher (not MPD) which throws some wrenches into our usual methods (e.g. hijacking ssh commands from mpirun) for setting up the mpi execute proxies on the execute nodes. For example, Hydra ignores duplicate hostnames in the machines file, and it checks the hostname of connecting proxies against the hostnames in the machines file, so we probably can't just put dummy hostnames in the machines file as we've done with Open MPI. There is maybe an opportunity to use a PMIx-based launcher/proxy system (does one exist?) instead of Hydra...? (see https://pmix.github.io/master/faq/ )

title: Ticket #7368: DAGMan should have option to evict jobs on MaxJobs changes
description: In #7236 we added the ability to edit properties of an in-progress DAGMan job, including the maximum number of running jobs (MaxJobs). In the current implementation, when a condor_dagman job gets edited so the new MaxJobs is lower than the number of currently running jobs, nothing gets evicted. We just won't submit any more jobs until the number of running jobs falls below the new maximum. Now we want the option for condor_dagman to evict jobs whenever we drop MaxJobs lower than the currently running number. A few details about this implementation: Jobs should get evicted in LIFO order (most recently started jobs get killed first). We'll need a new job attribute to determine whether jobs get evicted on changes. We'll call this DAGMan_EvictionPolicy or something similar. By default, jobs will not get evicted on changes. In addition, we realized the code that checks the job ad for attribute changes does not actually trigger as often as we thought. So a second piece of work is to isolate this code such that we have more control over how often it gets called. This is mostly just a minor refactor so I'm bundling it into this ticket instead of creating a new one.
remarks: 2020-Jan-08 11:54:18 by coatsworth: Hi all, I've completed the code to evict user jobs after reducing MaxJobs. It's pretty simple and straightforward. As for how an administrator opts in, there are two ways we could go about it. One is via a configuration knob. The other is by adding a new attribute in the job add that dictates what policy to use after modifying MaxJobs. title: Ticket #5705: Add NumJobCompletions to job ad.
description: Lauren has a customer whose desired job policy is "for a job to retry if it exits nonzero, but only five times, not counting evictions (which should cause the job to retry as usual)." As far as we can tell, this can't actually be done. It is possible that using NumShadowExceptions would get a closer approximation, inasmuch as the "eviction" above may also refer to a glide-in being killed. However, it shouldn't be too hard to have the shadow track the number of times the starter sent it an actual voluntary exit code and update the job ad appropriately. (It may be complicated by however it is that we handle the OOM killer and/or hard cgroup (memory) limits; I'm not sure.) This raises a question, however, about what to do about situations where the job's process completes (voluntarily exits) -- successfully or not -- but file transfer does not. I would assume that this user would like their job to retry, but that's without thinking too hard.
remarks: 2016-Jun-13 15:47:27 by tlmiller: The OOM killer puts things on hold, so that won't complicate anything. NumJobCompletions will be initialized to 0 to avoid unfortunate propogation of undefined. After speaking with Lauren, I confirmed that the user perspective is that if file transfer didn't complete, neither did the job. Still need to look into hard cgroup memory limits. 2016-Jun-13 15:50:36 by tlmiller: The testing for this could be rather extensive: for each of 'with file transfer on exit', 'with file transfer on exit or evict', and 'without file transfer', check that the NumJobCompletions changes by +1 on: exit 0, nonzero exit, and signal exit; and does not change on condor_hold, condor_vacate, condor_vacate_job, kill -9 starter, and kill -9 startd. (The last two should not depend on anything about file transfer, and so probably only need to be tried once each.) Not clear that we actually need all that, but it shouldn't be hard to do in the framework. 2016-Jun-13 16:18:19 by tlmiller: So it turns out that we hold on OOM kills only when using cgroups. However, having NumJobCompetions incremented by that is consistent with the wrong way the rest of HTCondor treats that case (as a "normal" SIGKILL, whatever that would be), so I won't worry about it. Hard cgroup memory limits also cause a job to go on hold, so that's not anything to be concerned about, either. 2016-Jun-15 10:24:37 by tlmiller: Converted testing needs into a new ticket, #5731, to give the student a swing at it.

title: Ticket #7738: Jobs on hold due to output and error files with permission ugo-rwx
description: When running with a shared filesystem under heavy load it has been repeatedly observed that jobs can end up on hold due to "Permission denied (errno 13)" for output and error files. For example, [root@ldas-pcdev6 ~]# condor_q -hold ... 54612769.0 jelle.urk 7/16 18:44 Error from slot1_16@node2088.cluster.ldas.cit: Failed to open '/home/jelle.urk/Projects/iDQ/NoVeto/observing/3/a/C00/chunk22_1253318003_1254009618_noidq_rerank/logs/gstlal_inspiral_calc_likelihood_inj_06B7-54612769-0.out' as standard output: Permission denied (errno 13) [root@ldas-pcdev6 ~]# ls -l /home/jelle.urk/Projects/iDQ/NoVeto/observing/3/a/C00/chunk22_1253318003_1254009618_noidq_rerank/logs/gstlal_inspiral_calc_likelihood_inj_06B7-54612769-0.out ---------- 1 jelle.urk jelle.urk 0 Jul 16 11:56 /home/jelle.urk/Projects/iDQ/NoVeto/observing/3/a/C00/chunk22_1253318003_1254009618_noidq_rerank/logs/gstlal_inspiral_calc_likelihood_inj_06B7-54612769-0.out One way to reproduce this is by submitting a large number of Vanilla universe jobs that direct output= and error= to an overloaded NFS shared filesystem and run condor_hold after a large number of transition to the Run state. title: Ticket #5210: condor_kbdd should not report transient mouse movement as 'activity'
description: It is complicated to write a policy for HTCondor that pays attention to deliberate mouse/keyboard activity but ignores unintended activity. The use of a SUSPEND policy is an attempt to deal with that, by suspending a job at the first sign of keyboard/mouse, and then evicting it only when the keyboard activity proves to be sustained. It would be much simpler if the keyboard daemon simply did not report transient activity at all. In particular it could ignore mouse movement that was not sustained over a configurable number milliseconds - but treat any keyboard activity as proof that a user was present. This would allow us to ignore the issue of transients when writing the startd policy.
remarks: 2015-Aug-13 11:56:01 by johnkn: two new config knobs control the sensitivity of this feature KBDD_BUMP_CHECK_SIZE number of pixels that the mouse can move in x and/or y while still being considered a 'bump'. i.e. if the movement is greater than this value then the move is not a transient and will register as activity. default is 16 pixels. setting this to 0 effectively disables bump testing. KBDD_BUMP_CHECK_AFTER_IDLE_TIME number of seconds of idle time before bump testing begins. default is 15 minutes. The algorithm is that after a period of idle time, if mouse movement is detected, and the mouse movement is less than KBDD_BUMP_CHECK_SIZE, then a second test is made for mouse movement after a 1 second pause. if the mouse is still moving, then the movement is reported as activity. if the mouse has not moved again, then the movement is ignored.

title: Ticket #4952: Improvements for LogReader API
description: A few things of note when trying to use the LogReader API in "real applications": There's no default constructor; you must explicitly feed it a filename. Should default to the JOB_QUEUE_LOG. No error reporting if fed an invalid file (i.e., no exception on EPERM). There's no event type corresponding to the CondorLogOp_LogHistoricalSequenceNumber. This makes log rotation detection impossible for the external script - the whole log must be processed upon startup. For example, if I want to run a cron job that periodically parses the log and uploads interesting events, I could write a separate state file containing the sequence number and offset of the last event processed. Then, on startup, if the sequence number matches, I could skip to the offset I care about. There might be some value to exposing the beginning and end of a transaction - but I'm not 100% certain there's a use case. A higher-level API which tracked the contents of ClassAds in memory (handling cluster/proc parentage and whatnot) would be less error prone. For example, something that emitted an event once per successful transaction containing the ClassAd at the beginning of the transaction and all the changes would be very useful. It's a useful API, but addressing the above would take out some of the sharp edges.

First, you can now use the following to define a macro: :macro-def:`MY_MACRO_NAME_DEFINITION` This will generate an anchor link (ie. /admin-manual/configuration-macros.html#MY_MACRO_NAME_DEFINITION) which can later be linked to. To set a generic anchor anywhere on a page, use the following syntax: :ref:`text I want to link to <my-anchor-name>` And then that text will be linkable at /my-page-url.html#my-anchor-name Let me know if this is enough to do what we need? For example - BZ#1081908 The kernel task scheduler could trigger a race condition while migrating tasks over CPU cgroups. The race could result in accessing a task that pointed to an incorrect parent task group, causing the system to behave unpredictably, for example to appear being unresponsive. This problem has been resolved by ensuring that the correct task group information is properly stored during the task's migration. BZ#1054072 Due to the locking mechanism that the kernel used while handling Out of Memory (OOM) situations in memory control groups (cgroups), the OOM killer did not work as intended in case that many processes triggered an OOM. As a consequence, the entire system could become or appear to be unresponsive. A series of patches has been applied to improve this locking mechanism so that the OOM killer now works as expected in memory cgroups under heavy OOM load. BZ#811255 The Out of Memory (OOM) killer killed processes outside of a memory cgroup when one or more processes inside that memory cgroup exceeded the "memory.limit_in_bytes" value. This was because when a copy-on-write fault happened on a Transparent Huge Page (THP), the 2 MB THP caused the cgroup to exceed the memory.limit_in_bytes value but the individual 4 KB page was not exceeded. With this update, the 2 MB THP is correctly split into 4 KB pages when the memory.limit_in_bytes value is exceeded. The OOM kill is delivered within the memory cgroup; tasks outside the memory cgroups are no longer killed by the OOM killer. 2014-Jul-28 14:31:40 by tim: Closing this due to the fact that an older kernel is most likely to blame.

title: Ticket #1603: Bug with spool subdir creation when named schedd config used
description: Using the named configuration stuff that's available in 7.4.2 to create multiple schedulers on a single machine I came across the following strange behaviour. This on Windows XP SP3. The pool has a shared file system. I created a single scheduler on my machine using the named scheduler approach that's available now (this is condor_config.local in attached tarball): SCHEDD1 = $(SCHEDD) SCHEDD1_ARGS = -f -local-name Q1 SCHEDD1_LOG = $(LOG)/ScheddLog.1 SCHEDD.Q1.SCHEDD_NAME = Q1@$(HOSTNAME) SCHEDD.Q1.SPOOL = $(LOCAL_DIR)/spool/1 SCHEDD.Q1.SCHEDD_LOG = $(SCHEDD1_LOG) SCHEDD.Q1.HISTORY = $(LOCAL_DIR)/spool/1/history SCHEDD.Q1.HISTORY_LOG = $(LOCAL_DIR)/spool/1/history DAEMON_LIST = $(DAEMON_LIST), SCHEDD1 Fairly straightforward and for the most part: this works just as planned. The weird behaviour comes when you run jobs. When I submit the attached test job with: condor_submit -name q1@winxpcm python.sub The jobs spool correctly, they even start and run correctly. But in the course of running a mirror set of cluster#.proc#.subproc# directories is created outside of the c:\condor\spool\1 directory and in the c:\condor\spool directory. It's mostly benign behaviour. Nothing ever gets spooled in those mirror directories. If I set leave_in_queue=true then the output is spooled in the c:\condor\spool\1 sub-directories for the jobs which is great. EXCEPT: the mirror directories that get created in c:\condor\spool never ever get cleaned up. They keep building and accumulating. Which means eventually they're going to not be benign anymore because they'll chew up inodes and make viewing that directory more and more of a pain. I'm not sure who is creating the mirror directories. It almost feels like it's the shadow daemons. The proper directories appear in c:\condor\spool\1 and then some time later, on the order 10 - 20 seconds, the mirror directories in c:\condor\spool show up. So not critical, but eventually anyone going with this approach is going to hit a wall as those directories, even though they're empty, do chew up disk resources. The attached archive contains the exact configuration files I used on this scheduler node (which was also my CM). I also included my job executable (a py2exe wrapped python script that dumps some info about the node and then sleeps) and the submit ticket I used to put it in the queue. Submit command is above. The screen captures show the state of the directories at two points in time: early one as the first few jobs from the 10 job cluster have started to run. And later, after all the jobs have completed.

title: Ticket #266: Old shadow: better failure detection when sending commands to StartD
description: This is part of the large patch set contributed by Dan Forrest. Dan's approach is to query the Collector and make sure the StartD's ad is there after sending the command. I'm not sure what failure mode this is protecting against. Commands are already sent to the StartD with TCP. Perhaps since the communication is one-way it's possible for a the Shadow to presume success when the StartD is hung but never actually reads the command? Chunks from the annotated diff of Dan's changes (which Todd has) that are associated with this ticket are labeled with a (16).
creator: gquinn

title: Ticket #4051: DaemonStartTime can't be used in DAEMON_SHUTDOWN expression
description: it turns out, that the DaemonStartTime attribute, as well as several other attributes are inserted into the daemon ad just before the ad is sent to the collector. This is AFTER the DAEMON_SHUTDOWN expression is evaluated. so DaemonStartTime cannot be used in this expression. We need to insert this attribute earlier, and stop using DCCollector::sendUpdate as a place to stuff attributes into the ad that are unrelated to the update process itself. In particular. DetectedCpus and DetectedMemory are also inserted into every ad passed to DCCollector::sendUpdate. These attributes don't even belong in every ad, and even if they were, DCCollector::sendUpdate is the wrong place to do that work.
creator: johnkn

title: Ticket #3794: glexec fails at Imperial College
description: Condor fails to use glexec at Imperial College, because condor_glexec_setup sets GLEXEC_TARGET_PROXY to a path that does not exist. This script doesn't actually want a target proxy to be created. The ability to turn off the target proxy by setting GLEXEC_TARGET_PROXY=/dev/null has been supported since glexec 0.9 (beginning of 2012). We believe it is an acceptable solution to depend on that. As far as I know, the only special thing about glexec configuration at Imperial is create_target_proxy=yes in glexec.conf.
remarks: 2013-Jul-19 13:59:56 by danb: Actually, glexec at Imperial College seems to be very different from the norm. I have tested at sites with create_target_proxy=yes, and this alone does not trigger the problem. Imperial may be using an entirely different implementation of glexec. I verified that the patch in condor that sets GLEXEC_TARGET_PROXY=/dev/null does successfully execute glexec jobs at Imperial.

title: Ticket #1253: condor_negotiator ran out of fds
description: The gist of the problem, from the ticket: Below is an excerpt from yesterday's NegotiatorLog on the Condor central manager at LHO. Rest of log is available, if needed. Cluster consists of 250 machines, 2000 slots, running CentOS 5.3, Condor 7.4.1 and there were 5000+ jobs being negotiated at the time. Negotiator was still working its way through the first 1000 before running out of FDs. I've since increased "nofile" from the default 1024 in /etc/security/limits.conf, and all seems fine. My question is, were there more than 1024 slots open for which the negotiator was negotiating? How many fds should the negotiator consume in normal operation? Is there a nonblocking tcp connect to each slot when looking for a match? Should we recommend the fd limits for negotiation machines be increased?

(get jobs), one per match (notify slot) Is there a nonblocking tcp connect to each slot when looking for a match? Yes, when a match occurs Should we recommend the fd limits for negotiation machines be increased? title: Ticket #6596: Share port daemon hanging on Debian 8
description: In the past week, the shared port daemon on the Debian 8 machine (exec-112.batlab.org) in the batlab has been hanging at least once a day. The master has to kill it to restore normal communication. In most cases, there's nothing interesting the shared port daemon's log. In one case, the daemon couldn't bind a socket to send its child alive to the master because there were no available ports in the configured port range of 9600-9700. When the shared port daemon enters this state, clients can connect and send an initial volley of data, but the connection isn't forwarded to the intended daemon and no data is sent back to the clients. This contributes to another bug (#6597), where a slot can become stuck in Claimed/Busy forever after a job completes. This problem started happening when Condor was upgraded from 8.4.4 to 8.6.6 on exec-112.batlab.org. The problem persisted when Condor was upgraded to 8.6.9. Other machines in the batlab that are running 8.6.9 don't show this behavior.

title: Ticket #7104: Custom resources sometimes not released from d-slot back to p-slot
description: If a non-fungible custom resource has more than one entry with the same name, when the second or subsequent instance of the resource should be released back to a p-slot when a d-slot is destroyed, the release fails. Subsequent attempts to create a d-slot using that resource will fail with the message ERROR "Failed to bind local resource '%s'" at line %d in %s For example if the following slot resources assignments exist startd classad fragments Name = "Slot1" SlotType = "Partitionable" AssignedGPUs = "CUDA0,CUDA0" GPUs = 0 Name = "Slot1_1" SlotType = "Dynamic" AssignedGPUs = "CUDA0" GPUs = 1 Name = "Slot1_2" SlotType = "Dynamic" AssignedGPUs = "CUDA0" GPUS = 1 And the STARTDs internal table of resource ownership will show CUDA0:1_1, CUDA0:1_2 When Slot1_2 is destroyed, the resource "CUDA0" will not be released back to the ownership of the p-slot - but the count of GPUs owned by the p-slot will still be updated. Only the first "CUDA0" will be released. So the situation will be startd classad fragments Name = "Slot1" SlotType = "Partitionable" AssignedGPUs = "CUDA0,CUDA0" GPUs = 2 And the STARTDs internal table of resource ownership will show CUDA0:1, CUDA0:1_2 Indicating that the p-slot owns 2 GPUS, but that the second "CUDA0" is assigned to slot1_2. Thus, when we try and hand out the second "CUDA0" resource to a new dslot, the assignment will fail and the STARTD will abort.
remarks: removal of the break is the fix, the rest is some D_FULLDEBUG logging to help diagnose problems in the future. 2019-Jun-20 08:48:07 by gthain: CODE REVIEW Looks good.

title: Ticket #2306: Multiple file logging output architecturally brittle
description: There are currently two problems with directing different debug levels to different log files. Both occur when someone tries to direct two debug levels to the same file for whatever reason. 1. The debug message is written twice in the log if the two debug levels are ORed in the dprintf call. 2. The current keep file open architecture would hold two file pointers to the same file. This means at rotation time we could conceivably attempt to rotate the file twice. The rotation code does close the file before reopening it for rotation purposes, but better just get rid of the duplicate handles in the first place. Proposed solution: Use a vector to store a struct that contains the path to the file, the file pointer, and the debug flags associated with that file. During configuration time the vector gets structs added to it as Condor discovers files for each debug level. During runtime a call to dprintf will sweep through the vectors and only ever write to a file in the vectors once in the run. This eliminates both problems. Long term this could probably be extended to include other "types" of output for dprintf.

title: Ticket #17: Add support for kernel threads to facilitate non-blocking i/o
description: Problem: US CMS has 10,000+ node glidein pools, and needs to authenticate all communications with GSI. Furthermore, these glidein pools have execute nodes all over the world, so network latency between collector and startd can be very large. When a startd first fires up, it takes 6 round trips w/ the collector to GSI authenticate - this can take more than a second. Most of this time (over 90% by our measurements) is spent down inside the gsi/ssl libraries blocked waiting on network I/O. The end result is currently as a workaround, CMS needs to run 20 collectors working together to handle a 10,000 node distributed glidein pool. :(. Proposed Solution: The time has come to add kernel-level threading to Condor. I know what you are thinking. Threads? Wtf? Todd, have you lost your mind? In a distributed system like Condor, adding threads will have us hunting down non-deterministic bugs for the rest of our lives!!! Don't fret, my fellow thread-fearing friends. The plan is to implement a threading model that is opposite of the traditional pthread idea. With pthreads, the basic idea is all threads run concurrently except for code that is explicitly marked as a critical section. Our plan here is to create a thread pool and only allow one kernel thread to run at a time, except in code sections that are explicitly marked as "thread safe". So in step one, the only code marked thread safe will be the network i/o kernel calls select(), send(), and recv(). Higher levels of the code will be able to easily turn threading on and off, which essentially says if Condor should yield a thread during network I/O or not. To solve the immediate problem, the solely the code in daemoncore which services the DC_AUTHENTICATE command will yield on I/O.

title: Ticket #1480: Remove node jobs that have been held "too many" times
description: DAGMan should remove any jobs that have gone on hold "too many" times. ("Too many" should be user-configurable.) (This came up because in the SIPHT workflows some jobs kept going on hold because of a problem with the executable, and for some reason the periodic remove expression was not working right, so the workflow got "stuck".)
remarks: 2010-Jul-01 15:35:26 by wenger: Hmm -- we have to think about how this will work for nodes that queue more than one job. (We can't easily keep track of the number of holds for each job proc, because we just have a data structure for the whole node.) 2010-Jul-01 15:40:47 by wenger: I just realized that the maxidle code probably won't work right for parallel jobs -- I think instead of a boolean flag for whether the node is idle, we need to keep a count of idle job procs, and compare that to the number of job procs that exist for the node... 2010-Jul-09 11:01:24 by wenger: Actually, I guess for parallel jobs, we should keep a hold count for each process, and if any process exceeds the limit, remove the whole cluster. Also, we need to remember to reset the count when re-trying a node. 2010-Jul-09 11:36:07 by wenger: I'm thinking of DAGMAN_MAX_JOB_HOLDS for the configuration macro. 2010-Aug-02 11:39:57 by wenger: This is going into the master branch, so I changed "fixed version" to v070504 (from v070404). 2010-Aug-27 12:39:03 by wenger: Committed code for this yesterday; I'm leaving the ticket open until I finish documentation. 2010-Aug-27 15:29:11 by wenger: This is now documented, so I'm going to resolve the ticket.

title: Ticket #5990: fix file creation on submit for "transfer_output_files"
description: Currently, empty files are created in the InitialDir for "transfer_output_files", stderr, and stdout. This creates the following issues: Issue 1. When empty files exist, even for stderr and stdout, users frequently think their jobs finished and that their executable created their intended output file, but didn't add any contents to it. This makes troubleshooting very difficult and adds to unnecessary user confusion. Issue 2. If the same filename is listed for "transfer_input_files" and "transfer_output_files", the input file is overwritten in the InitialDir with an empty file of the same name. This is REALLY bad. Proposed solution: Have HTCondor check for the pre-existence of the file (and check it's permissions?), and at least delete any empty files that are created, right after they're confirmed as writable.
creator: lmichael

title: Ticket #4682: win cmake script to copy the build results to to the release dir fails

title: Ticket #7807: Singularity should allow optional bind mounts
description: In an effort to remove the OSG User Job Wrapper scripts, we need to duplicate some of the wrapper script functionality in condor. One of the things the wrapper does is to run singularity with several directories on the host bind mounted insided the container, including /ceph /hdfds, /hadoop, /cvmfs. However, many sites don't have all these directories on the host. The existing user job wrapper, when given a list from the glidein startup string of potential directories to mount, only mounts those directories which exist on the host. Condor's singularity support can't do this (easily). If you give it a bind mount, it will unconditionally pass it to singularity, which will fail at startup time. We'll add a knob for condor to stat these directories, and only try to bind mount those which exist on the host.

title: Ticket #1195: Break recursive dependency between nightly.pl and condor_nmi_submit
description: One of the big vorticies of suckage in #974 is the chicken-and-egg dependency between nightly.pl, which builds our branches each night, and condor_nmi_submit (henceforth known as cns). The main problem is that a third party script produces a tags file on nmi-s006, then nightly.pl runs as a cronjob and checks out the master's copy of cns and runs it with the --nightly flag. Then, cns looks in the tags file, and for each branch checks out a copy of nmi_glue/SubmitInfo.pm, loads it for each branch, and submits the build. This is obviously problematic since it fixates the master's copy of cns as authoritative across all branches. This means a cns associated with a particular branch is not utilized. The way to fix it would be to have nightly.pl inspect the tags file and for each tag checkout the appropriate cns and whatever else it needs and just call the cns as necessary for each branch. This would get rid of the chicken and egg problem of which cns to use for the nightlies and go a long way to disentangling the horror of #974. The only problem at this point would be to make sure every revision of the cns treats its command line arguments the same way for nightly.pl. That is a restriction with which we can easily live and could probably be fixed if desired. Milestones 2010/05/11 Read the relevant code bases (nightly.pl, condor_nmi_submit) again. [DONE] Rewrite nightly.pl [DONE] Parse nightly tag file [DONE] Checkout a new copy of the nmi glue per tag [DONE] Submit a nightly build of Condor using that specific glue [DONE] Rip out old code from condor_nmi_submit. [DONE] Check it in to V7_4-branch and master. [DONE] Fix cron jobs to run the new nightly script. [DONE] Update the how to build on NMI pages for the new submission method. [DONE] Make sure I didn't break anything. [DONE]

title: Ticket #3901: Make draining attributes available to MAXJOBRETIREMENTTIME
description: Currently, MAXJOBRETIREMENTTIME is evaluated before any draining attributes are inserted into the resource ad. I'd like to implement the following policy: If preemption is due to draining, allow the job an additional N hours to leave. Otherwise, preempt immediately. Right now, this appears to be relatively impossible due to the lack of the draining attributes. The patch is straightforward - add the "Draining", "DrainingRequestId", and "LastDrainStartTime" attributes into the resource ads before the retirement time is calculated in ResMgr::startDraining. With this, the following works to implement my policy: MAXJOBRETIREMENTTIME = ifThenElse(Draining =?= true, LastDrainStartTime - JobStart + 24*3600, 0))

title: Ticket #2613: Add versioning to libcondor_utils
description: Now that the Condor utilities are stored in a shared library, there's the potential for a Condor binary to find the wrong version of the utilities library at run time, causing unexpected behavior. We should add some kind of versioning to prevent this from happening. I'm assuming that trying to track compatibility between different versions of Condor is infeasible. This is a private API that we change at will. We are happy to restrict a binary to work only with a libcondor_utils from the same release. There several options: Set the soname and increment on every release. Use symbol versioning for everything in libcondor_utils, with the version set to the Condor version. Include the Condor version in the filename (e.g. libcondor_utils-7.7.5.so).

title: Ticket #7411: Send fewer attributes in session resuming classad
description: When we resume a session, in either TCP or UDP, CEDAR looks up the session and sends the entire ClassAd. This is not necessary, and we really only need to send a subset of attributes that are ever potentially looked at. The list of attributes we need to send (because they are looked at) are: ATTR_SEC_USE_SESSION ATTR_SEC_SID ATTR_SEC_COMMAND ATTR_SEC_AUTH_COMMAND ATTR_SEC_SERVER_COMMAND_SOCK ATTR_SEC_CONNECT_SINFUL ATTR_SEC_COOKIE As Jaime pointed out, putClassAd can already take a projection so the code is quite straightforward.

Ticket #374: dlopen Kerberos
description: Kerberos causes us problems. We can't rely on every platform we support having it, but we want to support it whenever possible. We currently solve this by statically linking Kerberos into Condor. 1. This means we're stuck with an old version since newer version don't support static linking, 2. This means every Condor binary is carrying around Kerberos, bloating things. One possibility is to carry around the dynamic library with it, then use shell script wrappers on our binaries to set LD_LIBRARY_PATH. Lots of other packages do this. It's also messy. It is believed that our use of Kerberos is limited to a small number of functions. So the proposal is to use dlopen and dlsym to lead the Kerberos library and required functions at runtime. If dlopen doesn't work, we'll just disable the Kerberos code paths. Systems with the library will get Kerberos support, others won't. Condor will be smaller. We'll be able to use more more recent versions of Kerberos. If an admin upgrade Kerberos for a security fix, Condor will automatically get the benefit. Depending on how widely Kerberos is supported by Condor, we might want to look to the libtool dl library (ltdl) which provides portable wrappers for dlopen and dlsym, or at least to making our own wrapper. (Perhaps we have one already for our plugin work?) Note that #1135 ("Real" dynamic binary releases) offers another way to solve this. However, many users don't care about Kerberos at all, so this ticket remains an interesting option for all of the reasons given above. Or put another way: if you have the Kerberos libraries, it would Just Work, and if you didn't you wouldn't need to install one to make Condor happy, all while ensuring that Condor isn't shipping out of date and dangerous versions.

title: Ticket #4143: Python API mangles Requirements expression
description: When you submit jobs via the Python API, there are two problems with the way it updates the Requirements expression. (1) Requirements on `FileSystemDomain` and/or `HasFileTransfer` are added for all jobs, but they should not be added for scheduler universe jobs. The correct logic is in src/condor_submit.V6/submit.cpp, where check_requirements() doesn't add any file transfer requirements if mightTransfer(JobUniverse) is false. It only returns true for Vanilla, MPI, Parallel, Java and VM universes. However in the Python API, python-bindings/schedd.cpp make_requirements(), the should_transfer_files requirements (stf) are added regardless of universe. (2) When appending to the Requirements expression, the existing requirements expression is not enclosed in parentheses. This means that you can get some silly situations where for example Requirements = true || false expands to Requirements = true || false && TARGET.OPSYS == "LINUX" && TARGET.ARCH == "X86_64" && \ ( TARGET.HasFileTransfer || ( TARGET.FileSystemDomain == MY.FileSystemDomain ) ) && \ TARGET.Disk >= RequestDisk && TARGET.Memory >= RequestMemory and because && binds more tightly than ||, the additional requirements are cancelled. This behaviour is currently used as a workaround for problem (1): https://lists.cs.wisc.edu/archive/htcondor-users/2013-December/msg00104.shtml so better not fix this before fixing (1). The main driver for fixing (1) is so that you can submit DAGs programmatically. More discussion at https://lists.cs.wisc.edu/archive/htcondor-users/2013-December/msg00108.shtml and the thread containing it.
creator: b.candler

title: Ticket #2994: Have condor_defrag detect starvation
description: condor_defrag can effectively defragment the cluster, but it acts without regards to whether the cluster needs to be defragmented. What techniques are available to determine if there are any starved jobs out there? At a minimum, it seems like we should be able query the request_* attributes in the schedd and calculate whether it is possible for a job to starve. If it's not possible, we probably don't need to initialize draining. While I like the idea of p-slots, any user that puts in for a high-memory job on a busy cluster (read: all clusters that I know about), their job just seems to starve.

title: Ticket #1341: Rename "user log" to "event log" or possible "job event log"
description: The per-job log file is commonly called the "user log". This name goes all the way into the code, where the job's ClassAd points to the file with the name UserLog. However, it's confusing, as it's not a log of the user, it's a log of the job's events. Tellingly, the configuration setting to create a global user log file is EVENT_LOG, not USER_LOG. Calling it instead the "event log" or even more specifically the "job event log" would be much clearer. This will involve changes in the code to fix user visible usages (including UserLog), the documentation, and our daily language.

title: Ticket #6484: make public the code to buffer dprintfs for printing later
description: HTCondor has internal code for buffering dprintf() statements in memory and sending them to the log later. Typically, this is done to store the messages until such time that the debug subsystem has been properly initialized. However, this would also be useful in critical places where we need debugging information but can't write to the log. title: Ticket #231: ioctl(SIOCETHTOOL/GWOL) failed: Operation not permitted in pers condor
description: When running a green computing enabled condor that understands how to wake on lan in a personal condor situation, you get this in the log files: 2/20 13:41:27 ioctl(SIOCETHTOOL/GWOL) failed: Operation not permitted (1) This happens because Condor is trying to tinker with the ETHTOOL interface on the LAN device and can't because it doesn't have root permission. If the personal Condor administrator doesn't care about the WOL feature, they can ignore this error. Otherwise, if Condor is running as root and you see this error, it means something very bad happened with the WOL initialization and it likely won't work. In any event, the error message should be fixed, and potentially the WOL feature disabled at a higher level (with the disabling message being written to the log) if it is discovered there aren't good enough permissions to utilize it.

title: Ticket #3669: HOOK_JOB_EXIT always killed immediately by condor_starter
description:
There's a bug in condor_starter which affects the execution of a HOOK_JOB_EXIT. The bug causes the starter to terminate the hook immediately. If a job terminates the starter calls the function ShutdownGraceful in condor_starter.V6.1/baseStarter.cpp: The code piece if (!jobRunning) { dprintf(D_FULLDEBUG,"Got ShutdownGraceful when no jobs running.
"); this->allJobsDone(); return 1; } is erroneous as it reports that both job AND all hooks terminated when it returns 1. Returning 1 leads to immediate termination of the condor_starter and kills all running hooks. The correct version reads: if (!jobRunning) { dprintf(D_FULLDEBUG,"Got ShutdownGraceful when no jobs running.
"); return (this->allJobsDone()); } allJobsDone will return 0 if some hooks or other tasks are still running causing condor_starter to wait until they finished their work. I applied the fix to my version of condor and can confirm that it works. Here's the patch: --- src/condor_starter.V6.1/baseStarter.cpp +++ src/condor_starter.V6.1/baseStarter.cpp @@ -365,12 +365,11 @@ } ShuttingDown = TRUE; if (!jobRunning) { dprintf(D_FULLDEBUG, "Got ShutdownGraceful when no jobs running.
"); - this->allJobsDone(); - return 1; + return (this->allJobsDone()); } return 0; } Update Dec. 2013: Turns out that my patch fixes the case of normal termination (i.e. the job ends on its own) but not the case wher a user aborts the job. In this case again the hook gets right after it has been started. This other bug is in jic_shadow.cpp as it seems. Here's a patch solving this problem as well: --- src/condor_starter.V6.1/jic_shadow.cpp 2013-12-02 21:38:52.000000000 +0100 +++ src/condor_starter.V6.1/jic_shadow.cpp 2013-12-02 21:34:48.000000000 +0100 @@ -382,7 +382,7 @@ r2 = updateShadow( &update_ad, true ); } - return r1 || r2; + return (r1 && r2); }
remarks: 2014-Jan-17 12:28:14 by tannenba: CODE REVIEW Thanks for the patch. Looks good, except in JICShadow::allJobsDone, I think we only want to consider r1(the result from parent class allJobsDone()) in our return code. I don't think a failure to update the shadow here should result in stopping the starter from exiting, because there will not be another external event. I think it should just return the status of r1, like it used to be before commit [28760] - specifically, I think this change introduced this bug in the first place. 2014-Jan-17 13:33:09 by gthain: CODE REVIEW Looks good.

title: Ticket #1654: getrlimit() broken in stduniv
description: getrlimit() is broken in stduniv. See the rust ticket. I discovered that some backwards compatibility code in the CEDAR code for the rlimit structure was breaking the 64-bit transfer of the RLIM_INFINITY value. While coverage testing, I found that the 32-bit version was also broken in that we used __NR_getrlimit on the i386 kernel, which is 2gb limited (and produced the same output on 32-bit linux as the 64-bit problem, but for completely different reasons). I changed it to use __NR_ugetrlimit on the i386 kernel since that can handle up to 4gb and also RLIM_INFINITY properly.

title: Ticket #4456: Shared port daemon steadily leaking file descriptors
description: When SharedPortClient::PassSocket() invokes SharedPortState::Handle() in non-blocking mode, the unix domain socket created by SharedPortState is never closed(). This happens when the shared_port daemon sends a child-alive message to the master. Consequently, the share_port daemon leaks a file descriptor every 20 minutes. With the default 1024 fd limit, the daemon run out of fds and crash after 13 days. The fix is to delete the ReliSock containing the unix domain socket when SharedPortState::Handle() is done and is in blocking mode.

title: Ticket #4905: Avoid matchmaking schedds near limits
description: When a schedd is near its resource limits (i.e., near the MAX_JOBS_RUNNING), it will still send large resource requests to the negotiator. For example, CMS has a schedd with an autocluster of size 70,000. The schedd is running 19,999 jobs (MAX_JOBS_RUNNING is set to 20,000). It will still happily send out the resource request to the negotiator - in our case, the negotiator sends back 4,000 matches; the schedd drops them on the floor. Because the glideins aren't used, they eventually exit - causing significant churn. There are other schedds in the pool that have plenty of capacity - it's just that this problematic one eats up all the potential matches. I propose a two-pronged fix: New config variable, CURB_MATCHMAKING. This is an expression which is inserted into the schedd ad. When this evaluates to true, we do not offer any new resource requests to the matchmaker. Adjust the resource request count to be no more than max_offers = (MAX_JOBS_RUNNING - # shadows running). Prevent more than max_offers job requests from being outstanding with the negotiator at any time in the asynchronous protocol.
remarks: 2015-Mar-19 16:57:52 by tannenba: Code Review Nice patch, thanks! Looks good. Merged to master. 2015-Mar-19 17:07:23 by tannenba: Regression testing thoughts... (for bill) In condor_config set MAX_JOBS_RUNNING = 2 Then submit 100 jobs with queue 100 so that all jobs end up in the same autocluster. Should then see a line in the ScheddLog that says 03/19/15 15:34:31 Offering 2 jobs instead of 100 to the negotiator for this cluster; nearing internal limits (MAX_JOBS_RUNNING, etc).

title: Ticket #6892: credmon(s) should run under the credd

title: Ticket #2582: Document QUEUE_SUPER_USERS macro
description: The QUEUE_SUPER_USERS macro is not defined in the manual from what I can see. It should be discussed in the security section. In the documentation about WRITE level authorization in the schedd, the following is mentioned: The commands which write information into the job queue (such as condor_submit and condor_hold). Note that for most commands which attempt to write to the job queue, Condor will perform an additional user-level authentication step. This additional user-level authentication prevents, for example, an ordinary user from removing a different user's jobs. I believe this is referring to the QUEUE_SUPER_USERS mechanism, but I can't find a clear description anywhere else. I would note that the QUEUE_SUPER_USERS mechanism is completely unlike the rest of the authorization mechanisms - it's based on the user name, not the domain name or the originating address. This breaks the security scheme at our site, where we make a distinction between daemons (foo@daemon.unl.edu) and site users (username@unl.edu).
creator: bbockelm

title: Ticket #6742: Undefined job policy expressions should result in default action
description: Today, if a job policy expression evaluates to Undefined, the job is held with a reason code indicating the policy expressions are faulty. Users can easily end up in this situation when referencing attributes that aren't always present in the job ad (e.g. attributes that only appear when the job is in certain states or once the job starts running for the first time). This seems overly hostile to the user. This should be changed so that the default behavior is performed when the value is Undefined (i.e. don't hold job, don't release job, let completed job leave queue).

title: Ticket #6312: Protocol errors in negotiation
description: I noticed there were quite a few high-priority CMS workflows on one schedd queued up for Nebraska but not running. Further, low-prio jobs from other schedds were starting to run: this was starting to ring some alarm bells. Looking at the problem schedd, I saw lots of negotiation that looked like this (from SchedLog): 06/21/17 03:48:21 (pid:9979) Activity on stashed negotiator socket: <negotiator:1097> 06/21/17 03:48:21 (pid:9979) Using negotiation protocol: NEGOTIATE 06/21/17 03:48:21 (pid:9979) Negotiating for owner: production.cmsdataops@cms 06/21/17 03:48:21 (pid:9979) Negotiating owner=production.cmsdataops@cms jobprio restricted, min=900000 max=900000 06/21/17 03:48:21 (pid:9979) Checking consistency running and runnable jobs 06/21/17 03:48:21 (pid:9979) Tables are consistent 06/21/17 03:48:21 (pid:9979) Rebuilt prioritized runnable job list in 0.040s. 06/21/17 03:48:22 (pid:9979) Finished negotiating for production.cmsdataops in local pool: 0 matched, 16 rejected 06/21/17 03:48:22 (pid:9979) Activity on stashed negotiator socket: <negotiator:1097> 06/21/17 03:48:22 (pid:9979) Negotiator command was 425 (not NEGOTIATE_WITH_SIGATTRS or NEGOTIATE) --- aborting From the negotiator side, it would try to negotiate for prio 900k jobs -- succeed but produce no matches -- then negotiate for prio 600k jobs from the same user. However, when done with prio 600k, it would get a generic socket failure. It seems like the schedd and negotiator disagree where they are in the protocol. Command # 425 from the negotiator is END_NEGOTIATE, but schedd thought it already finished negotiating. It seemed to be blocking the prio 600k jobs so I did a qedit of all the stuck workflows to set JobPrio = 900000: they immediately started running, again pointing to a negotiation problem. My working theory is there is a problem in the negotiator when prefetching is enabled and global job prios are used, causing it to send the END_NEGOTIATE command twice. Looking through the Negotiator logs for socket write failures, it seems to occur with every busy schedd.
remarks: 2017-Jun-21 16:40:59 by jfrey: My simple attempts to reproduce this error have been unsuccessful. The logs indicate that the schedd considered the negotiation over without receiving an END_NEGOTIATE command (otherwise, it would log "Lost priority - X jobs matched"). It only does this if it receives SEND_JOB_INFO or SEND_RESOURCE_REQUEST_LIST and immediately responds with NO_MORE_JOBS. This implies that prefetch didn't get all of the request ads. The negotiator asked for more during the regular cycle, and after it got them all, sent a superfluous END_NEGOTIATE. I've yet to find a way to trigger that set of events. Could I get login permission on one or more of the affected submit machines? 2017-Jun-21 21:17:30 by bbockelm: I'm not sure about a login, but here's some output from the NegotiatorLog: 06/22/17 03:44:29 Negotiating with production.cmsdataops@cms at <scheddA:4080?addrs=scheddA-4080&noUDP&sock=7892_d584_3> 06/22/17 03:44:29 0 seconds so far for this submitter 06/22/17 03:44:29 2 seconds so far for this schedd 06/22/17 03:44:29 USE_GLOBAL_JOB_PRIOS limit to jobprios between 600000 and 600000 06/22/17 03:44:29 Request 16236.00113: autocluster 4 (request count 1 of 427) 06/22/17 03:44:29 Rejected 16236.113 production.cmsdataops@cms <scheddA:4080?addrs=scheddA-4080&noUDP&sock=7892_d584_3>: no match found 06/22/17 03:44:29 Request 16604.00001: autocluster 27 (request count 1 of 2) 06/22/17 03:44:29 Rejected 16604.1 production.cmsdataops@cms <scheddA:4080?addrs=scheddA-4080&noUDP&sock=7892_d584_3>: no match found 06/22/17 03:44:29 Request 16604.00003: autocluster 51 (request count 1 of 2) 06/22/17 03:44:29 Rejected 16604.3 production.cmsdataops@cms <scheddA:4080?addrs=scheddA-4080&noUDP&sock=7892_d584_3>: no match found 06/22/17 03:44:29 Request 16604.00005: autocluster 160 (request count 1 of 2) 06/22/17 03:44:29 Rejected 16604.5 production.cmsdataops@cms <scheddA:4080?addrs=scheddA-4080&noUDP&sock=7892_d584_3>: no match found 06/22/17 03:44:29 Request 16607.00007: autocluster 12 (request count 1 of 2) 06/22/17 03:44:29 Rejected 16607.7 production.cmsdataops@cms <scheddA:4080?addrs=scheddA-4080&noUDP&sock=7892_d584_3>: no match found 06/22/17 03:44:29 Request 16628.00003: autocluster 47 (request count 1 of 2) 06/22/17 03:44:29 Rejected 16628.3 production.cmsdataops@cms <scheddA:4080?addrs=scheddA-4080&noUDP&sock=7892_d584_3>: no match found 06/22/17 03:44:29 Got NO_MORE_JOBS; schedd has no more requests (... snip ... lots of other negotiating, another pie spin) 06/22/17 03:46:36 Group production - BEGIN NEGOTIATION 06/22/17 03:46:36 Phase 3: Sorting submitter ads by priority ... 06/22/17 03:46:36 Starting prefetch round; 29 potential prefetches to do. 06/22/17 03:46:36 Starting prefetch negotiation for production.cmsdataops@cms. 06/22/17 03:46:36 USE_GLOBAL_JOB_PRIOS limit to jobprios between 50900000 and 50900000 06/22/17 03:46:36 condor_write(): Socket closed when trying to write 655 bytes to schedd production.cmsdataops@cms, fd is 62 06/22/17 03:46:36 Buf::write(): condor_write() failed 06/22/17 03:46:36 Failed to send submitterName/eom to production.cmsdataops@cms (<scheddA:4080?addrs=scheddA-4080&noUDP&sock=7892_d584_3>) 06/22/17 03:46:36 Failed to prefetch resource request lists for production.cmsdataops@cms(<scheddA:4080?addrs=scheddA-4080&noUDP&sock=7892_d584_3>). Here's the corresponding ScheddLog: 06/22/17 03:44:26 (pid:2972902) Activity on stashed negotiator socket: <negotiator:28694> 06/22/17 03:44:26 (pid:2972902) Using negotiation protocol: NEGOTIATE 06/22/17 03:44:26 (pid:2972902) Negotiating for owner: production.cmsdataops@cms 06/22/17 03:44:26 (pid:2972902) Negotiating owner=production.cmsdataops@cms jobprio restricted, min=900000 max=900000 06/22/17 03:44:28 (pid:2972902) Finished negotiating for production.cmsdataops in local pool: 0 matched, 63 rejected 06/22/17 03:44:28 (pid:2972902) Increasing flock level for production.cmsdataops to 2 from 0. 06/22/17 03:44:29 (pid:2972902) Activity on stashed negotiator socket: <negotiator:28694> 06/22/17 03:44:29 (pid:2972902) Using negotiation protocol: NEGOTIATE 06/22/17 03:44:29 (pid:2972902) Negotiating for owner: production.cmsdataops@cms 06/22/17 03:44:29 (pid:2972902) Negotiating owner=production.cmsdataops@cms jobprio restricted, min=600000 max=600000 06/22/17 03:44:29 (pid:2972902) Checking consistency running and runnable jobs 06/22/17 03:44:29 (pid:2972902) Tables are consistent 06/22/17 03:44:29 (pid:2972902) Rebuilt prioritized runnable job list in 0.045s. 06/22/17 03:44:29 (pid:2972902) Finished negotiating for production.cmsdataops in local pool: 0 matched, 6 rejected 06/22/17 03:44:29 (pid:2972902) Activity on stashed negotiator socket: <negotiator:28694> 06/22/17 03:44:29 (pid:2972902) Negotiator command was 425 (not NEGOTIATE_WITH_SIGATTRS or NEGOTIATE) --- aborting Note the timestamps - the schedd hung up on the negotiator at 03:44:29, but the negotiator didn't notice this until 03:46:36. 2017-Jun-26 15:19:44 by jfrey: The negotiator not noticing the closed connection for two minutes isn't surprising. It's going to ignore the socket until the next time it wants to talk to that schedd. 2017-Jun-30 12:58:35 by jfrey: The problem is related to prefetching, but not global job priorities. It can be triggered when there are multiple request ads for the some autocluster, due to interleaving job priorities. When prefetch gets all of the request ads and the last ad is in the same autocluster as a previous ad that didn't get matched, the negotiator sends an extra SEND_RESOURCE_REQUEST_LIST (which won't return any new ads) followed an unnecessary END_NEGOTIATE (which the schedd isn't expecting). In ResourceRequestList::getRequest(), if the boolean m_send_end_negotiate is true, then prefetch saw a NO_MORE_JOBS from the schedd and the negotiator shouldn't try to fetch any more request ads. The function should return false immediately if there are no more ads (cached_resource_request is exhausted and m_ads is empty). We check this once before trying to pull another ad from m_ads. But if the remaining ads in m_ads are in autoclusters that have already been exhausted, the function ends up querying the schedd for more ads when it shouldn't. If the schedd responds with NO_MORE_JOBS (the usual case), it will consider the negotiation complete. But the calling function in the negotiator thinks it still needs to send an END_NEGOTIATE. The check of m_send_end_negotiate needs to move inside the while loop looking to populate front. 2017-Jul-03 09:18:01 by bbockelm: Great detective work! Can I request a backport to the stable series also? While not essential for CMS, I think it sounds like other users of prefetching might also trigger this problem. If this clears out all the prefetch errors, then maybe (in a separate ticket) we should consider turning it on by default. 2017-Jul-31 15:08:52 by johnkn: CODE_REVIEW change looks good. I believe that this change makes this code just before the while loop unnecessary // The prefetch of RRLs saw a NO_MORE_JOBS from the schedd. // Hence, once m_ads is empty and we run out or resource_request_count, // then we ought to return false. // // In this case, we never ask the schedd to send job info, so we must // send an explicit END_NEGOTIATE to inform it we are done. if (m_send_end_negotiate && m_ads.empty()) { return false; } 2017-Sep-06 14:04:23 by jfrey: I agree that indicated code above the loop is unnecessary after this change.

title: Ticket #2351: Ensure CREAM lease exists before submitting job in gridmanager
description: When submitting a CREAM job, the CreamJob object in the gridmanager will skip checking the value/validity of the CREAM lease (maintained in the CreamResource object) if CreamLeaseId is set in the job ad. This can lead to the submission failing because the lease isn't registered on the server. The CreamJob object should always check with the CreamResource about the value of the lease id and its status before attempting to submit. When information about a previous submit attempt is scrubbed from the job ad in GM_CLEAR_REQUEST, CreamLeaseId should be removed.
remarks: 2011-Aug-15 13:32:17 by tannenba: IIRC, part of this is to deal w/ leveraging the capability of CREAM to share one lease across multiple jobs.... 2011-Aug-22 14:30:16 by jfrey: It appears the bug in this ticket can't occur as described. The CreamLeaseId attribute is never set, so it can never be used in the CreamJob constructor to set leaseId and bypass asking the CreamResource for the id of the lease. #2271 may be causing the behavior observed with this ticket. I'm waiting on Rod Walker to try out the fix for that ticket. 2011-Oct-18 16:47:40 by jfrey: I found a race condition in CreamResource that would explain this behavior. CreamResource won't hand a lease id to CreamJobs via getLeaseId() until m_sharedLeaseExpiration is set to non-zero. But in UpdateLeases(), m_sharedLeaseExpiration is set to the calculated lease value, then control is returned to daemonCore to let the value be saved in the schedd, then CreamResource talks to the server to register it. While CreamResource is waiting for the value to be saved in the schedd, CreamJob objects may try to submit if daemonCore timers fire at the right time. A new guard variable needs to be added to getLeaseId() so that the lease id is returned only after the initial registration of the lease with the server is complete. 2011-Oct-19 14:14:51 by jfrey: I've sent a patched gridmanager to Rod Walker for testing. 2011-Dec-01 15:37:47 by jfrey: This bug can also be triggered by the gridmanager retaining CreamResource objects for several minutes after they have no associated jobs (controlled by GRIDMANAGER_EMPTY_RESOURCE_DELAY). During that time, the CreamResource object won't extend the job lease, as it has no jobs to base the length on. I saw a case with glideinwms where a problem job would become held immediately after it was released, which occurred once a minute due to the job policy expressions. This prevented the CreamResource object from ever being deleted. But each time it checked on job leases, it had no jobs and so never extended the lease, which eventually expired. After that, any new jobs would fail on submission because the lease was invalid. Setting GRIDMANAGER_EMPTY_RESOURCE_DELAY=5 broke the loop, as the CreamResource object was deleted before the next time the problem job was released. 2011-Dec-05 14:01:32 by jfrey: I've pushed a patch to V7_6-branch and posted a pre-release binary for Rod Walker, Xin Zhao and Igor Sfiligoi to try: ftp://ftp.cs.wisc.edu/condor/temporary/forrod/2011-12-01/condor_gridmanager 2012-Jan-06 14:32:34 by jfrey: Rod Walker reports that lease problems have not reoccurred since installing the patched binary.

title: Ticket #3813: shared port should be enabled by default
description: NOTE: CHILD TICKETS MUST BE RESOLVED BEFORE THIS TICKET IS RESOVLED To make it easier for HTCondor to work in private networks, we want the shared port feature to be enabled by default. We also want it to use a specific port number by default, rather than a dynamic port number. Design doc at https://docs.google.com/document/d/1UMz24DG1rOsMfKqiOzo_nSEXIGcRHAfdNuzEI-Wv5vQ/edit?usp=sharing
remarks: 2013-Jul-30 14:15:41 by tannenba: Re how to handle the collector: Another idea would be for the shared port daemon to automagically forward any "undecorated" connection to the collector. This would get around the backwards-compatibility problem with folks needing to change CONDOR_HOST, and it would also enable all HTCondor nodes to use just the one well-known 9618 port by default (instead of requiring two ports on the cm, one for the shared port service and one for the collector). Dan, what do you think re the above? What would it take? (2 hours, 2 days, 2 weeks?) 2013-Jul-30 16:46:39 by danb: Very roughly, I think it would take about a week of effort to iron out all the details of transparently handling the collector. UDP is one issue. One way to deal with it would be to have the shared port server not listen on the UDP port, so the collector can listen on it directly. This "half shared port" mode will require a little mucking around to get right, but I can't think of any major roadblocks. That just leaves TCP, which should be straightforward. I suppose we could even forward SOAP requests. Are there any cases of commands where it would be ambiguous whether that command should go to the shared port server or to the collector? How about signals under windows? I suppose the master could send signals to the shared port server via TCP, and to the collector via UDP. Seems a little fiddly. How about DC_AUTHENTICATE? The only thing I can think of that needs to authenticate to shared_port is the master when it sends signals in windows. These days, children are born with a security session for this purpose, so I don't think this case presents a problem. 2013-Dec-30 18:34:37 by bbockelm: Branch posted to https://github.com/bbockelm/htcondor/tree/default_shared_port (note that this is on top of the non-blocking shared port code in #4094). I took tannenba's suggestion to have shared_port forward all unknown commands (which works out to be all commands except the shared_port command and DC_RAISESIGNAL) to a default shared port ID. You need to add the following to the config: SHARED_PORT_DEFAULT_ID=collector COLLECTOR_ARGS = -sock collector SHARED_PORT_ARGS = -p 9618 USE_SHARED_PORT = true (I'd like to use TJ's new param table voodoo to get these to be set automatically as matt suggested in #2622, but couldn't figure it out...) For UDP, I set the shared_port to not use UDP. If the collector is set to use the shared port, then the master gives the collector the UDP port but a randomly-selected TCP port. Signals are not forwarded from the shared_port to the collector; as no new authentication session is ever needed, we never have to worry about the fact we do forward DC_AUTHENTICATE requests to the collector. The master sends signals to the collector via the collector's dedicated UDP socket. TCP updates are trivially handled; UDP updates first cause an authentication session to be created via TCP (forwarded from the shared_port) then the collector's UDP socket is used for the actual update. I don't forward SOAP requests. 2013-Dec-30 19:16:38 by bbockelm: Ok, the configuration gymnastics drove me a bit nuts... I added "COLLECTOR_USES_SHARED_PORT" (defaulting to true). If this is set and USE_SHARED_PORT=true, then the rest of the configuration is done automatically. So basically we just need to default USE_SHARED_PORT to true and the whole stack should "just work". 2014-Mar-29 20:23:18 by bbockelm: Hi Todd, Now that 8.1.5 freeze has been made, should we work to merge this branch in for 8.1.6? Brian 2014-Jul-11 10:54:41 by bbockelm: Ok, I re-merged master into this branch and resolved all the conflicts. Should be in a reasonable state for review again. 2014-Jul-15 14:31:39 by bbockelm: Code Review (from Todd and Jaime on phone) EXCEPT if SOAP is enabled and shared port is. Double-check if shared port is using 9618. Keep this as default on all platforms. WOULDBENICE: someone needs to simplify the crazy Create_Process argument list. Who is responsible for cleaning up the shared port files? Note: after phone call, Brian confirmed condor_preen does this. WOULDBENICE: Would be nice to use anonymous domain sockets instead. Add version history WOULDBENICE: Investigate upping the file descriptors to shared port. Note: this was done for v8.3.0 in commit [40637] Update the design doc. WOULDBENICE: Remove reply for shared port except on Mac OS. Document new param knobs. Once the concrete action items are (so, excluding WOULDBENICE items), this can be merged. 2014-Jul-23 08:43:25 by bbockelm: Review items were fixed in follow-up commits. The only big deviation is I did not set this as default on Windows; batlab test failures appeared to reveal a threading issue and I'm not really qualified to fix (I haven't owned a copy of Windows for quite some time...). NOTE NOTE NOTE: One thing we overlooked in the original review is that this represents a pretty key behavior change. Worker nodes and submit nodes will now use port 9618 by default. This is going to upset glideins; accordingly, I introduced a new parameter, SHARED_PORT_PORT, which controls the default port used by shared port (otherwise, you have to muck with the SHARED_PORT_ARGS -- not very friendly). The default of SHARED_PORT_PORT is 9618; admins can set it to 0 to restore the prior behavior. This configuration will be superseded by the collector port if the master launches a collector.

title: Ticket #7446: Enable condor_fetchlog with fine-grained auth
description: Currently, condor_fetchlog contacts a remote daemon and performs a command to fetch the contents of a logfile. With the introduction of fine-grained authentication, we do not envision startds acting as servers and establishing a new security session as the startd host has only a fine-grained token and not the password file. We should take the lead from how the schedd / negotiator relationship currently works - the condor_master could advertise a capability to the collector and pre-register it as a security session. Then, any connection coming from that specific security session will be pre-authorized to fetch the log.
remarks: 2020-Jan-10 16:08:52 by tlmiller: Results of our Thursday (2020-01-10) meeting (as I recall them): Code to advertise a fine-grained capability should move into daemon core. (Off by default.) We should take this opportunity to improve our forward-compatibility with respect to private attributes; some new attribute prefix should always be private. We should think about startd flocking while implementing and this reviewing this; the first consequence is that we need a way to determine which collectors are trusted. We should merge the patch which makes checking a socket for authorization a single function call. We still want to explain this to Zach and have him review the idea (and, probably, some of the code).

title: Ticket #1438: Addition of skip_filechecks to condor_submit language
description: skip_filechecks provides the writer of a submit file control over the checks condor_submit will perform on files, such as input and output. It allows fine-grain control that was previously only available in configuration via SUBMIT_SKIP_FILECHECKS or on the command line via condor_submit's -disable flag. For example, if it is desirable to have condor_submit verify the existence of input files for only one job the following can be done, executable = EXE input = input_that_must_already_exist queue skip_filechecks = true input = input_that_will_exist queue This is also useful for users of DAGMan, where it is not possible to tell DAGMan to pass -disable to condor_submit and disabling all filechecks via SUBMIT_SKIP_FILECHECKS is either infeasible or undesirable.

title: Ticket #5882: $ENV in config/submit should support defaults
description: when $ENV() is used to fetch an environment variable that is not defined, it expands to UNDEFINED. This works ok when $ENV() is used inside a $$() expansion in a submit file, but is pretty useless otherwise. The $ENV() syntax should be enhanced to support a default value after a : in the same way the $() and $$() expansions do. $ENV(var:default) would expand to the value of the var environment variable if var is defined and non-empty, it would expand to default otherwise. some examples: $ENV(HOME) - expands to a users home directory or UNDEFINED $ENV(HOME:/home/nobody) - expands to a users home directory or /home/nobody $ENV(HOME:) - expands to a users directory or the empty string

title: Ticket #1068: HAD is confused by private network info
description: The following address comparison in the HAD code gets confused if there is any extra information packed into the daemon contact string: if(strcmp( sinful_addr, my_sinful ) == 0 ) { This results in the following message from HAD: my address '<128.105.143.12:51450?PrivNet=cs.wisc.edu.internal>'is not present in HAD_LIST This showed up in a pre-release of 7.4.1 because the fix for #973 caused private network information to be consistently advertised in the way that was intended when the handling of private network info was revised in 7.3.0. Two fixes should be made: HAD should use Sinful::addressPointsToMe() to do the address comparison properly. The private network name should only be published if it is really needed. If there is no private address or CCB information, it is not needed. This reduces the scope of other bugs similar to the one in HAD and it allows us to retain backward compatibility with Condor prior to 7.3.0 in more cases.
