title: Ticket #1804: ClassAdList assumes ownership of ads
description: In old classads, there was a convoluted system for reference counting to manage memory when a classad belonged to multiple ClassAdLists. When the compatibility implementation of ClassAdList was made for new ClassAds, this appears to have inadvertently been dropped. The result is that when an ad belongs to multiple lists and the destructors of those lists are invoked, the ad will be deleted multiple times, likely causing the program to crash. Brian Bockelman has observed crashes of the negotiator due to a bad free in ClassAdList::~ClassAdList. This could be a result of the bug described above. I have been able to produce a crash of the negotiator caused by this problem by using the following configuration: GROUP_NAMES = physics GROUP_QUOTA_DYNAMIC_physics = 0.5 The problem also appears if I do not define a quota at all. It does not appear if I define GROUP_QUOTA_physics to something > 0. The reason is that when there is a static quota defined, the negotiator appears to manage the submitter ads in a way that avoids the ads remaining in two ClassAdList objects when those objects are destroyed. The job that I submit to cause the problem doesn't have to even be a member of any group. Example: executable = /bin/sleep arguments = 3600 notification = never queue Valgrind reports the following error in the negotiator: ==29756== Invalid read of size 4 ==29756== at 0x81EC5BE: compat_classad::ClassAdList::~ClassAdList() (compat_classad_list.cpp:51) ==29756== by 0x811BD06: Matchmaker::negotiationTime() (matchmaker.cpp:1373) ==29756== by 0x8145A29: TimerManager::Timeout() (timer_manager.cpp:413) ==29756== by 0x812EF1C: DaemonCore::Driver() (daemon_core.cpp:3092) ==29756== by 0x81268E7: main (daemon_core_main.cpp:2356) ==29756== Address 0x44b5330 is 0 bytes inside a block of size 100 free'd ==29756== at 0x4005234: operator delete(void*) (vg_replace_malloc.c:346) ==29756== by 0x8220CD8: compat_classad::ClassAd::~ClassAd() (compat_classad.cpp:684) ==29756== by 0x81EC5D1: compat_classad::ClassAdList::~ClassAdList() (compat_classad_list.cpp:51) ==29756== by 0x81142A1: Matchmaker::SimpleGroupEntry::~SimpleGroupEntry() (matchmaker.cpp:1389) ==29756== by 0x811BA9E: Matchmaker::negotiationTime() (matchmaker.cpp:1342) ==29756== by 0x8145A29: TimerManager::Timeout() (timer_manager.cpp:413) ==29756== by 0x812EF1C: DaemonCore::Driver() (daemon_core.cpp:3092) ==29756== by 0x81268E7: main (daemon_core_main.cpp:2356) How to Fix One option would be to add reference counting. To do this right, we would need to consistently use it in all places where pointers to ClassAds are passed around. We could cheat and only apply it in the case of ClassAdList, but I think this is unexpected. For now, I am just adding a second version of the class called ClassAdListDoesNotDeleteAds. One should only ever put a classad in a single ClassAdList. It can exist in multiple instances of ClassAdListDoesNotDeleteAds. The only place I have found where this new class needs to be used is in the negotiator for the startd and schedd ads.
remarks: 2010-Dec-12 16:05:41 by danb: It is likely that Brian's problem was not due to the bug described in this ticket. Instead, it is likely that it was caused by my changes in #1773 that made ClassAdList incompatible with shallow copying as done by qsort of arrays in the negotiator containing ClassAdList.

title: Ticket #7483: condor_q -dag <id> should display nested dags
description: Currently, we can use the following command to display a condor_dagman job and the jobs nested under it: condor_q -nobatch -dag <id> However this will only show the jobs running immediately under that particular id. If there are any subdags in the workflow, anything nested deeper than the first level will not appear. It's important to note that it is currently possible to display nested dags by simply omitting the ID of the condor_dagman job: condor_q -nobatch -dag However this also produces a lot of output about other jobs that we don't care about. We should change condor_q to show the full list of nested jobs when specifying the job ID. One way to do this is for condor_dagman to publish a new attribute in the job ad of the root dagman ID, so we can run a constraint about this. TJ also suggested an implementation involving the schedd. We should agree on an approach before moving forward with this.

title: Ticket #3993: Replace rescue DAG with recovery mode?
description: ToddT and I have talked about possibly replacing rescue DAGs with recovery mode, since rescue DAGs are really just an optimization. That would mean we wouldn't have to maintain two separate mechanisms with similar functionality. There are a few issues we need to think about: Recovery mode is possibly more "fragile" -- the data in the node job log file(s) is wiped out if you start up in non-recovery mode. (Possibly this could be dealt with by saving copies of the workflow log file.) Startup would be slower (parsing the log file is slower than parsing a rescue DAG). (We should quantify how much slower.) If we do this (or maybe even if not) we should have some capability that replicates the '-do_rescue' flag -- maybe something like this: condor_submit_dag -recovery <workflow log file> ... time
remarks: 2013-Oct-21 15:40:42 by pfc: Just to be pedantic, rescue DAGs are not just an optimization -- they are also insurance. There have been times when recovery failed but we were able to restart from a rescue DAG. If we had #3889 (or some other form of periodic DAG state "backups") then I would be comfortable considering rescue DAGs to be simply an optimization.

title: Ticket #2681: parallel universe broken on dynamic slots (request_cpus is ignored)
description: Resolved ticket as this issue was addressed in #2808 [This is copied from two emails by Steffen Grunewald <Steffen.Grunewald@aei.mpg.de> to the CondorLIGO list.] Getting closer with Parallel Universe on Dynamic slots... but still no cigar. The setup consists of 5 4-core machines and some more 2-cores machines. All of them have been configured as single, partitionable slots. Preemption is forbidden completely. The rank definitions are as follows: RANK = 0 NEGOTIATOR_PRE_JOB_RANK = 1000000000 + 1000000000 * (TARGET.JobUniverse =?= 11) * (TotalCpus+TotalSlots) - 1000 * Memory I'd expect this to favour big machines over small ones (for Parallel jobs), and partially occupied ones over empty ones. What I see with the following submit file, is quite different: universe = parallel initialdir = /home/steffeng/tests/mpi/ executable = /home/steffeng/tests/mpi/mpitest arguments = $(Process) $(NODE) output = out.$(NODE) error = err.$(NODE) log = log notification = Never on_exit_remove = (ExitBySignal == False) || ((ExitBySignal == True) && (ExitSignal != 11)) should_transfer_files = yes when_to_transfer_output = on_exit Requirements = ( TotalCpus == 4 ) request_memory = 500 machine_count = 10 (mpitest is the ubiquitous "MPI hello world" program trying to get rank and size from MPI_COMM_WORLD) if I leave the Requirements out, the 10 MPI nodes will end up on the big 5 machines (one per machine) plus 5 small ones with the Requirements set as above, each of the big machines will run exactly two nodes instead of 4+4+2+0+0 not all out.* and err.* files get written (the pattern looks semi-random) all of them identify as "rank 0" of "size 1" Condor version is 7.6.0 (and should include the fixes of ticket 986 which went into 7.5.6). How can I debug this? === It turns out that request_cpus=n, independent of n, will result in one slot claimed per machine, as I could prove with "request_cpus=4" and "machine_count=4" which claimed a single slot on four machines, same as would "request_cpus=1" or "request_cpus=2" would have done. "machine_count" obviously gets translated into the number of individual MPI jobs (nodes), and "request_cpus" would define the number of CPU cores assigned to each of them. It's my problem if the nodes don't know about multi-core on their own. Apparently, dynamic slot provisioning doesn't work well with parallel universe yet. As soon as I return to old-style slot splitting (NUM_SLOTS=4, cpu=1, memory=25%, etc.) I get the "proximity" I'm looking for - of machine_count=10, the first 4 nodes get sent to one node, 4 to the next one, 2 to another. So I either do hard partitioning, and get proper MPI behaviour, or dynamic partitioning, and am able to run memory-hungry jobs. Unfortunately, the users have been asking for both (and the mix is unpredictable). To add to the inconvenience, for each reconfig Condor has to be stopped completely on the machines affected. Are there plans to make Condor more flexible? Using up as many dynamic slots as possible on the same machine would help a lot. In the manual, and everywhere else I looked, "dynamic slots" and "parallel universe" seem to be disjoint concepts... BTW: If there was proper co-existence of dynamic slots and parallel universe, one would have to look for a N_P_J_R expression that yields best results for the parallel job while harming as little other jobs as possible - perhaps such a thing doesn't even exist if preemption is allowed? Without preemption things should be easier: - Rank by number of unclaimed CPUs? How to do that? have another machine ClassAd attribute UnclaimedCpus? I vaguely remember someone had come up with a huge ifThenElse construction to sum up the resources "bound" by claimed dynamic slots, but there should be a solution that still works for 64 cores...)
remarks: 2011-Dec-02 16:36:34 by tstclair: Could have sworn this has been fixed. 2011-Dec-09 08:56:04 by matt: See also, https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=545423 2011-Dec-15 17:10:53 by eje: Fixing this requires making some mods to the negotiator. Make the computation of available resources ("pie") more aware of partitionable slots (a sort of extension to the fix for #2440). To achieve the desired "packing" of machines, the negotiator loop needs logic to allow matching more than one job to a partitionable slot ad. Currently the negotiation loop cycles through the slot ads, under the (incorrect) assumption that one job can be matched to one ad. Fixing this would also improve non-parallel matching performance, since a partitionable slot could match against more than one job per negotiation cycle. 2011-Dec-16 10:57:00 by eje: Making the necessary changes to the negotiation logic seems a bit risky for stable series, especially on short notice and w/out better regression testing. title: Ticket #6904: USER_JOB_WRAPPER should execute outside singularity container

remarks: 2019-Feb-07 12:27:35 by bbockelm: Can we document why we think this is the correct decision? (Not saying that it is wrong, but just would like to leave breadcrumbs for future Brian...) 2019-Feb-07 12:43:13 by gthain: The administrator who deploys the USER_JOB_WRAPPER, may not know at configuration time, what the image the singularity container will use. As such, the admin can't put the USER_JOB_WRAPPER into the container. title: Ticket #7616: condor_q -submitters should honor accounting groups
description: The -submitters argument to condor_q queries the collector for all of the submitter records matching a given a name. When there are multiple schedds, there can be multiple submitter records. it then queries each schedd with a constraint Owner=="name" , this works fine when the submitter is an actually an owner, but for jobs that have an AccountingGroup attribute, the submitter name is actually the value of the AccountingGroup attribute. So it would be more correct for condor_q to use this constraint (AccountingGroup?:Owner)=="name" . (For older schedds this will have to be written (AccountingGroup is undefined ? Owner : AccountingGroup)=="name"

title: Ticket #5781: add caching of script output to config include command
description: It is a common use pattern to have a config file include the output of a command, but to want to capture that output to a file after the first run and then use the resulting file for subsequent parsing of the config. This is especially important if only one process can safely run the command at the same time. It is possible to work around this by using a combination of config if statements and temporary config variables, like this. example condor_config REQUIRE_LOCAL_CONFIG_FILE = false LOCAL_CONFIG_FILE = $(LOCAL_DIR)/stuff.config, $(LOCAL_DIR)/condor_config.local example condor_config.local if ! defined STUFF # stuff.pl writes "STUFF=1" to stdout and to $(LOCAL_DIR)/stuff.config include command : perl $(LOCAL_DIR)/stuff.pl endif But this mechanism is a bit hard to use, especially for RPM users. It would be better to have a first-class mechanism to declare that config files do not have to exist and to have config write the output of a script to a file and then use the file. To do this two new keywords will be added to the include : statements in config (and submit) files: into and ifexist include [ifexist] command [into <cache-file>] : <cmdline> include [ifexist] [into <cache-file>] : <cmdline> | include [ifexist] : <file> The into keyword must be followed by the full pathname of a file to write the output of the script into, If that file exists, it will be read and the script will not be executed. If that file does not exist, the output of the script will be written into it and then it will be read. If the script produces no output, a zero length file will be created. If the script returns a non-zero error code, configuration will abort and the cache file will not be created unless the ifexist keyword is also specified. Also, two new keywords will make it possible to deal with script errors in a more deterministic way. error : error message warning : warning message So the above example would become any config file # stuff.pl writes "STUFF=1" to stdout include into $(LOCAL_DIR)/stuff.config : perl $(LOCAL_DIR)/stuff.pl if ! defined stuff error : stuff is needed! endif It should be noted that the automatic configuration variables $(IsMaster) and $(CondorIsAdmin) can be used to help insure that the cache file is written only by a rootly daemon if that is needed, something like this any config file if $(IsMaster) include into $(LOCAL_DIR)/stuff.config : perl $(LOCAL_DIR)/stuff.pl if ! defined stuff error : there must be stuff! endif else include ifexist : $(LOCAL_DIR)/stuff.config endif In the future, it might be good to have a way to pass an argument to condor_reconfig to request that all scripts be run even if the cache files exist.

title: Ticket #2044: Dynamic slots in OWNER state won't be removed
description: (Description copied from https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=691969; John has a patch for this issue, and I'll be reviewing and integrating it.) Description of problem: If I setup dynamic slot and configure it to run only special job by job attitude, for example: NUM_CPUS=8 SLOT_TYPE_1 = cpus=8 SLOT_TYPE_1_PARTITIONABLE = TRUE NUM_SLOTS_TYPE_1 = 1 START = TARGET.JobIsSpecial=?=True Then when a special job is submitted: Executable=/bin/sleep Arguments=20 Universe=Vanilla +JobIsSpecial=True should_transfer_files = YES when_to_transfer_output = ON_EXIT queue The dynamic slot would be created to run the job. It is because the dynamic slot will be in Owner state because of the START expression, but from the source code dynamic slot only change to delete state from Unclaimed state.

title: Ticket #3655: restarting procd on failure doesn't retry correctly
description: The latest changes to the code for #3618 prevent restarting the procd in an infinite loop when the daemon can't establish a connection to the restarted procd. However, if procd startup fails early (before it closes the stderr pipe back to the parent), we will EXCEPT and not actually retry as many times as intended. And perhaps EXCEPT is not the best course of action in general for this case.

title: Ticket #4485: Testing with shared port on - impact
description: What happens to our test runs when shared port is on? First thing we encountered was string for the daemon ports being too long and though brian is patching this I needed an immediate test method. For now the testing framework uses a shorter path in /tmp and hopefully cleans it at the end of the test run. That folder is stored in the file SOCKETDIR in condor_tests. Workstation tests have to recreate this file and contents to run . condor_view_classad_types.run was broken because it only tried to parse a non-shared port address but not parses either. job_services_during_neg_cycle.run broke because running with the shared port true displays a bug where userprio calls now again wait for the end of the negotiation cycle. lib_ccb_schedd.run and lib_ccb_startd.run fail because what they expect to see as chatter within the collector log doen's happen with the shared port daemon handling things. The last three are fixed for now by their turning off the shared port daemon for the condors they configure and run.
remarks: 2014-Jul-24 19:54:35 by bbockelm: You shouldn't need to manually set the DAEMON_SOCKET_DIR for tests anymore - the condor_master will do this automatically if it detects the path is too long. See #4465.
check_ins: 2014-Jul-24 12:25 Check-in [40751]: When the shared port daemon is requested, in our test framework the path is to long to open the daemon shared port socket. We now relocate the daemon directory to a unique folder in /tmp/tds$$. When we are done with a run, we remove it. We place this unique path into condor_tests/SOCKETDIR and CondorPersonal.pm [...] (By Bill Taylor )
creator: bt

title: Ticket #2802: schedd not always reusing claims when it should
description: Found a bug in the schedd that causes it to release claims when it still has jobs it could run on those claims. The problem arises when a job no longer matches a slot after it completes - this is not all that uncommon using our defaults w/ dynamic slots. The story is: a job id x completes. schedd goes through priorec array to try and find another job that matches the claimed resource. UNFORTUNATELY, it may happen that (a) the priorec has yet been rebuilt (i.e. using a cached priorec array), and (b) the job classad for complete job id x has not yet been destroyed, as it is waiting to be destroyed in the enqueueFinishedJob queue as a result of a and b, findrunnable job will try to match the very job that just completed with the now idle claim the job that just completed may no longer match with the claimed startd ad, especially in the case of submitting jobs w/ the defaults and using dynamic slots. For instance, machine.Memory < jobad.ImageSize, because ImageSize in the completed job is now bigger than when the resource was initially claimed (because now that the job is completed, ImageSize now reflects the real size seen by the starter and not just the size of the executable on disk). findrunnable job now marks the entire autocluster as not matching this claim the claim is relinquished when Todd's test really expected it should be reused :(
remarks: 2012-Feb-01 11:01:32 by tannenba: Pushed patch [30063] that fixes the problem by changing the order of our checks in schedd FindRunnableJob(). Previously, this method first tested that the job and machine ad still matched, then tested that the job is still runnable. I reversed the order - first test that the job is still runnable, then test that it matches. This prevents FindRunnableJob() from considering a job that just completed (step 3 above), which is what got us into trouble in the first place. 2012-Feb-01 13:09:05 by matt: This is unlikely to impact anyone who is using RequestMemory. The default when not is very small, almost guaranteed to be overrun and trip this issue. 2012-Feb-03 15:45:53 by tstclair: So in testing this at length, I've found there appears to be numerous times where we release a claim that could have been matched. I'm still tracing the logic to identify the cases. I found that we never re-use a claim until it times out. I'm reopening as a result. 2012-Feb-06 14:41:45 by tstclair: I'll reopen if once I can find a consistent repro method, moving on for now.

title: Ticket #2101: inconsistent lookup of attributes in a transaction
description: I noticed in 7.6.0 that nice_user accounting is inaccurate, because the "User" attribute in the job ad is missing the nice-user prefix, so the usage gets attributed to the wrong accounting record. It appears that a change in the 7.5 series caused the code that handles the insertion of the nice-user prefix to be exposed to an ancient bug in the way the schedd handles lookup of ad attributes that have not yet been committed. In GetAttributeInt(), if the attribute has been modified in the current transaction, the result is computed via the following: sscanf(attr_val, "%f", val); There is no error checking to see if the value was actually an integer. For example, if val was 123.99 * 1000 the answer would be 123. More relevant to the nice-user problem, if val was true, the answer would be 0, whereas if the attribute was not modified in the current transaction, true would instead yield the integer value 1. Similar problems affect GetAttributeFloat(), GetAttributeBool(), GetAttributeStringNew(), and GetAttributeString(). The solution is to let the classad library generate the answer rather than trying to implement our own parser in qmgmt.
remarks: 2011-Apr-29 15:34:37 by jfrey: This changes the return values of the GetAttribute...() functions. Before, they returned -1 on failure, 1 if the value was modified in the active transaction, and 0 otherwise. I don't think any callers care about the distinction the 0 and 1, but we should preserve it for the stable series.

title: Ticket #1404: Bad ldap server can make nordugrid_gahp exit
description: The nordugrid_gahp exits when it receives a SIGPIPE. The assumption is that a SIGPIPE indicates that one of the pipes to its client has been closed. However, a NORDUGRID_LDAP_QUERY command issued to a misconfigured ldap server can also result in a SIGPIPE. This is because a SIGPIPE is generated when the process writes to a closed pipe or socket. Igor Sfiligoi had his nordugrid_gahp exit unexpectedly when attempting to query an ldap server that closed connections immediately after they were opened. The connections stayed open long enough for the ldap library to start sending data, triggering a SIGPIPE. The solution is for the nordugrid_gahp to ignore SIGPIPE and exit if writing to stdout fails with EPIPE. Fortunately, virtually all writes to stdout are funneled through gahp_printf(), which makes adding a check easy.
remarks: 2010-May-13 11:54:22 by jfrey: Pushed a fix to V7_4-branch for 7.4.3. The nordugrid_gahp now ignores SIGPIPE and exits if writes to stdout fail with EPIPE.

title: Ticket #6791: Chained spooling of job sandbox between schedds fails
description: ATLAS reported a failure when attempting to submit a Condor-C job using condor_submit -spool. The job goes on hold in the second schedd with a complaint that it can't access job files under a path within the first schedd's spool directory. This is a bug between how the gridmanager constructs the new job ad for a Condor-C job and how the schedd rewrites the job ad when the job sandbox is spooled. When a job's sandbox is spooled to the schedd, the schedd rewrites the job ad to change file paths so that they point to the files' new locations under the SPOOL directory. The original values of the modified attributes are saved under new attribute names with a SUBMIT_ prefix. These are used when the output sandbox is transferred back to the submitter. If the attribute SUBMIT_Iwd is already set, then the schedd skips the rewriting process, under the assumption that it has already done the rewriting. When the gridmanager submits a Condor-C job to a remote schedd, it doesn't remove attributes with a SUBMIT_ prefix in the job ad that it sends to the remote schedd. If the local schedd has rewritten the job ad, then the remote schedd will not rewrite, even though it should. Thus, the remote schedd will attempt to access files using paths that are relevant to the local schedd.

title: Ticket #4256: param self-references to pre-defined param values don't work
description: Normally, when the parameter in the config file refers to itself the self-reference is substituted at config load time. so foo = 2 foo = $(foo) + 1 in the second line above, $(foo) will be replaced with 2 at the time the config file is read, and foo -> 2 + 1 will be written into the config table. But when the current value of foo comes from param_info.in instead of an earlier line in the config file, then $(foo) will be substituted with "" instead of the pre-defined foo. The result is that config file params can't build on pre-defined values for the same param.

title: Ticket #2678: RFE: expose accounting group negotiation-ordering to configuration
description: Motivation is twofold: 1) Customers have been requesting a return to legacy behavior of "none" group such that it negotiates last (instead of its current behavior of being ordered in with other groups by starvation) 2) There have been some other requests that indicate a desire to explicitly control the negotiation order of accounting groups in customer-dependent ways The proposed solution to both of these cases is to expose an accounting group ordering expression to configuration that would return some floating point number that would be used for acct groups. Supporting this feature would require the creation of a classad for each accounting group, populated with some attributes that could be used for expressions. Some obvious candidates would be: Name # acct group name StarvationRatio # current starvation ratio Quota # assigned slot quota Allocated # actual slots allocated (not to be confused with quota) Usage # current group usage Priority # group's priority PriorityFactor # group's priority factor One possible config scheme would be to work analogously to the other group quota settings, so there would be a default sort expression: # none goes last, otherwise default sort by quota-denominated starvation GROUP_QUOTA_SORT_EXPR = ifThenElse(Name=?="<none>", 1e100, Usage/Quota) And then optional group-specific ones: # Group a always goes first GROUP_QUOTA_SORT_EXPR_a = -10 # group b always goes 2nd GROUP_QUOTA_SORT_EXPR_b = -9 Or you could explicitly order all of them: # Group a always goes first GROUP_QUOTA_SORT_EXPR_a = 1 # group b always goes 2nd GROUP_QUOTA_SORT_EXPR_b = 2 # ... GROUP_QUOTA_SORT_EXPR_z = 26 # anybody else goes at the end, sorted by acct group prio GROUP_QUOTA_SORT_EXPR = 27 + Priority
remarks: 2011-Dec-01 13:42:36 by eje: Or, maybe: GROUP_SORT_EXPR GROUP_SORT_EXPR_<groupname> 2011-Dec-07 16:55:57 by eje: Attached patch that exposes a new config param: GROUP_SORT_EXPR, which can be set to a classad expression that involves any of: "Name" - accounting group name "Quota" - the slot quota assigned during this neg cycle "Requested" - the number of slots being requested by the submitters in the group "Allocated" - the number of slots allocated by the HGQ algorithms "Usage" - the slots currently in use by this accounting group "Priority" - the accounting group's priority "PriorityFactor" - the group's priority factor The expression must evaluate to a numeric value, or it will be defaulted to FLT_MAX with a warning message in the negotiator log. GROUP_SORT_EXPR defaults to backward-compatible starvation-ratio sorting expression: 'ifThenElse(Allocated>0.0,Usage/Allocated,3.40282e+38)' (note, it was decided to defer on providing group-specific expressions of the form GROUP_SORT_EXPR_<groupname>, pending feedback from customers) 2011-Dec-07 17:07:46 by eje: TESTING: Using the following configuration: NEGOTIATOR_DEBUG = D_FULLDEBUG NEGOTIATOR_USE_SLOT_WEIGHTS = FALSE NEGOTIATOR_INTERVAL = 30 SCHEDD_INTERVAL = 15 CLAIM_WORKLIFE = 0 NUM_CPUS = 10 # turn off round robin and multiple allocation rounds HFS_ROUND_ROBIN_RATE = 100000000 HFS_MAX_ALLOCATION_ROUNDS = 1 GROUP_NAMES = a, b GROUP_QUOTA_a = 5 GROUP_QUOTA_b = 5 GROUP_AUTOREGROUP = TRUE # sorts "b" before "a": GROUP_SORT_EXPR = ifThenElse(Name=?="a", 2, ifThenElse(Name=?="b", 1, 3.40282e+38)) # this should trigger warnings and default to FLT_MAX: #GROUP_SORT_EXPR = 2+"a" Bring up the negotiator with the above configuration, and then observe the ordering behavior for group negotiation: $ tail -f NegotiatorLog | grep -e WARNING -e sortkey 12/07/11 14:44:43 Group b - sortkey= 1 12/07/11 14:44:43 Group a - sortkey= 2 12/07/11 14:44:43 Group <none> - sortkey= 3.40282e+38 Next, enable GROUP_SORT_EXPR = 2+"a", which defaults with warnings: $ tail -f NegotiatorLog | grep -e WARNING -e sortkey 12/07/11 14:39:41 WARNING: sort expression "2+"a"" failed to evaluate to floating point for group <none> - defaulting to 3.40282e+38 12/07/11 14:39:41 WARNING: sort expression "2+"a"" failed to evaluate to floating point for group a - defaulting to 3.40282e+38 12/07/11 14:39:41 WARNING: sort expression "2+"a"" failed to evaluate to floating point for group b - defaulting to 3.40282e+38 12/07/11 14:39:41 Group <none> - sortkey= 3.40282e+38 12/07/11 14:39:41 Group a - sortkey= 3.40282e+38 12/07/11 14:39:41 Group b - sortkey= 3.40282e+38 Disable the settings for GROUP_SORT_EXPR, and let it take on its default "starvation-order" expr. Submit the following file: cmd = /bin/sleep args = 60 should_transfer_files = if_needed when_to_transfer_output = on_exit +AccountingGroup="a.user" queue 5 +AccountingGroup="b.user" queue 10 You should see something similar to the following sequence, where prior to submission, all values are FLT_MAX, then "a" and "b" have zero starvation-ratio, as their allocation is nonzero but no jobs are yet running. Then their starvation ratios will become 1, as all allocation is filled. Then "a" will empty as its jobs complete first, then finally all ratios will return to FLT_MAX: $ tail -f NegotiatorLog | grep -e WARNING -e sortkey 12/07/11 15:33:31 Group <none> - sortkey= 3.40282e+38 12/07/11 15:33:31 Group a - sortkey= 3.40282e+38 12/07/11 15:33:31 Group b - sortkey= 3.40282e+38 12/07/11 15:33:51 Group a - sortkey= 0 12/07/11 15:33:52 Group b - sortkey= 0 12/07/11 15:33:52 Group <none> - sortkey= 3.40282e+38 12/07/11 15:34:23 Group a - sortkey= 1 12/07/11 15:34:23 Group b - sortkey= 1 12/07/11 15:34:23 Group <none> - sortkey= 3.40282e+38 12/07/11 15:34:53 Group a - sortkey= 1 12/07/11 15:34:53 Group b - sortkey= 1 12/07/11 15:34:53 Group <none> - sortkey= 3.40282e+38 12/07/11 15:35:23 Group b - sortkey= 0 12/07/11 15:35:24 Group <none> - sortkey= 3.40282e+38 12/07/11 15:35:24 Group a - sortkey= 3.40282e+38 12/07/11 15:35:54 Group b - sortkey= 1 12/07/11 15:35:54 Group <none> - sortkey= 3.40282e+38 12/07/11 15:35:54 Group a - sortkey= 3.40282e+38 12/07/11 15:36:24 Group b - sortkey= 1 12/07/11 15:36:24 Group <none> - sortkey= 3.40282e+38 12/07/11 15:36:24 Group a - sortkey= 3.40282e+38 12/07/11 15:36:55 Group <none> - sortkey= 3.40282e+38 12/07/11 15:36:55 Group a - sortkey= 3.40282e+38 12/07/11 15:36:55 Group b - sortkey= 3.40282e+38 2011-Dec-16 18:11:58 by tannenba: CODE REVIEW Thanks for the patch!!! Nice job. Just a few items: Fix the memory leak on this line: string group_sort_expr = param("GROUP_SORT_EXPR"); --- you prolly wanna use param(string value,const char*name) instead. Use EvalFloat() instead of LookupFloat() on this line: if (!ad->LookupFloat(ATTR_SORT_EXPR, v)) { --- although lookup is currently implemented in terms of eval, it may not stay that way forever. Lets try and make the attribute names come close to matching up the attribute names used by the PREEMPTION_REQUIREMENTS expr. So instead of ATTR_NAME for the attribute name describing the group, use ATTR_ACCOUNTING_GROUP. Instead of "Allocated", use "GroupResourcesInUse", etc. Some questions: Not sure I understand fully the difference between Allocated and Usage. Will Allocated > Usage always be true? I.e. Usage is what the account says, and Allocated is what the accountant says plus what we hope will be true after this negotiation cycle? Was this tested using dynamic group quotas? Does the value of the "Quota" attribute move around if the user is using static quotas? If I set group_quota_a = 5 group_quota_b = 10 GROUP_SORT_EXPR = ifThenElse(Name=?="<none>", 1e100, Usage/Quota) then is it true that the none group will get 0 machines until group a has 5 and group b has 10? 2011-Dec-19 09:16:53 by eje: Thanks for the feedback! Regarding (3), I can use the styles of attribute names from the PREEMPTION_REQUIREMENTS, although it seemed a bit redundant since in the context of this feature since by definition all attributes pertain to groups for GROUP_SORT_EXPR (e.g. why make the user say GroupResourcesInUse when they can just say Usage, etc). The difference between Allocated and Usage: Usage is just the resources currently used by all submitters in the group. "Allocated" is how many resources that were just allocated by the HGQ algorithms. Some definitions (to be included in doc): "Quota" is the resource quota assigned by HGQ, always in units of slots (possibly weighted, etc): If it's a static quota, it will (normally) be exactly the static quota from the config file (unless the static quotas are greater than available resources, in which case they are normalized with a warning) If it was a dynamic quota, "Quota" will be the (dynamic quota) * (available resources). "Requested" is basically (running+idle) jobs - that is, how many jobs would this group run if it could. "Allocated" is how many resources (in units of slots) were the given to the group by the HGQ algorithm. Allocated can be > Quota, if the group received some surplus. It can be < Quota, if Requested < Quota. Note, this is why I defined the starvation-ratio as Usage/Allocated, instead of Usage/Quota. Testing w/ dynamic quotas is more or less moot, since the Quota the sorting algorithm cares about is whatever comes out of HGQ. The HGQ treatment of static/dynamic quotas has been tested elsewhere (but should eventually get into regression suite) Regarding "GROUP_SORT_EXPR = ifThenElse(Name=?="<none>", 1e100, Usage/Quota)", that sort-expr will make sure that "<none>" negotiates last. So, groups "a" and "b" will get get first shot at negotiation. Technically, that does not absolutely guarantee they get what they want, but if they don't get it, it will be because of a failure to match slots, etc, not because somebody in "none" got there first. 2011-Dec-20 15:47:05 by johnkn: The sense of this seems backwards to me. Where smaller numbers are used to give groups HIGHER priority. It would be more consistent with the the rest of condor for this to be a RANK expression for the groups. With the current behavior resolving to something like. GROUP_RANK_EXPR = ​ifThenElse(Group=?="<none>",​ 0,​ ​ifThenElse(Allocated ​> ​0,​ Quota/Allocated,​ Quota*2)​)​ 2011-Dec-22 15:28:49 by eje: Regarding the proposal for using the name 'GROUP_RANK_EXPR': the group negotiation order is most similar to the submitter negotiation order, which is governed by priority that is sorted from smallest to largest value. Possibly it could be called GROUP_PRIO_EXPR, although the sorting expression given doesn't need to have anything to do with priority as the Accountant defines it. 2011-Dec-27 14:48:29 by johnkn: After some discussion Todd and TJ strongly feel that the default value for 7.7.x should be SORT_EXPR = "Usage/(Quota+1)" And we also wonder whether any current user of 7.6.x actually depends on the algorithm that treats all groups as having equal sort order (at the end)until they get their first allocation; And then sorts groups that have resources before groups that don't.

title: Ticket #1957: Node job failure/retries/slow aborted event/recovery mode cause error
description: The following combination of events results in a fatal error in DAGMan: 1) A node job failed (killed by a signal). 2) DAGMan saw the terminated event for the job, and re-submitted it, because retries were turned on for that node. 3) After the re-submission, an ABORTED event for the first job was written to the user log. 4) DAGMan went into recovery mode and re-read the events that resulted from steps 1-3. (When not in recovery mode, the scenario above at least usually results in a non-fatal error; in recovery mode it's fatal because of changes in the timing of seeing the various events.)

title: Ticket #93: gridmanager's job polling near job completion can be improved
description: BNL was having a problem where jobmanagers were failing to send job DONE updates to the gahp. In the job RSL, the gridmanager sets the gram commit timeout to 10 minutes, so the jobmanager will wait that long for a reply to its DONE message before exiting. BNL had set the gridmanager’s active job poll interval to 20 minutes, so by the time the gridmanager tried to poll the jobs’ status, the jobmanagers were long gone. The resulting error on the gridmanager’s eventual poll attempt should cause it to attempt restarting the jobmanager. But it may be nice to catch the problem earlier by ensuring the commit timeout for the job is longer than the gridmanager’s poll interval.
remarks: 2009-Jun-17 14:18:58 by jfrey: This feature is already implemented by commit [10037]. Not sure why BNL was having this problem.

title: Ticket #1812: shorten lifespan of delegated proxies
description: When condor delegates proxies in Condor-G and in vanilla universe, it should shorten the lifespan of the delegated proxy. This would allow the user to have a long-lived proxy on the submit machine but only send short-lived proxies to the remote sites. There should be a schedd-wide configuration knob to control the lifespan of delegated proxies. The job should be able to override this. The default should be 24h. The proxy will need to be re-delegated periodically to avoid expiration. This should be done by default at intervals of 1/4 of the delegated lifespan.
remarks: 2011-Jan-27 17:34:12 by danb: I implemented this feature for Condor-C and non-grid universes. As implemented, there is a new configuration setting DELEGATE_JOB_GSI_CREDENTIALS_LIFETIME which specifies the maximum number of seconds delegated credentials should be good for. The default is one day. The job can override this setting with its own setting of DelegateJobGSICredentialsLifetime. Renewal of the credential is attempted as before (i.e. when the proxy on the submit node is updated) and periodically every 0.25 of the desired lifetime of the delegated proxy. This schedule is adjustable with DELEGATE_JOB_GSI_CREDENTIALS_REFRESH, which defaults to 0.25. The precision of the timing (and therefore the maximum rate of updates) can be controlled with SHADOW_CHECKPROXY_INTERVAL, which defaults to 600 (10 minutes). When the proxy is delegated, the job ClassAd attribute DelegatedProxyExpiration is set to the timestamp when the delegated proxy will expire. Jaime and I looked into adding support for Globus, but we did not see a straightforward way to do it, at least in gt2; the globus interfaces we are using do not support specifying a lifetime, so either we would need to patch the globus library and expose some methods that are not public, or we would need to delegate the credential twice: once internally in the memory of the gahp_server where we would shorten its lifespan, and then the usual delegation to the remote server. I'm hoping we come up with a better option, because neither of those sounds very good. If we do, we should open a new ticket for that work. I have not added a built-in mechanism that puts the job on hold when the remote proxy expires. This could be done with a periodic hold expression that references DelegatedProxyExpiration while the job is running. 2011-Jan-28 15:22:08 by danb: There is one thing left to understand in this ticket: when using glexec, the shadow delegates a proxy to the startd in order to get things started. As implemented, this delegation has a limited lifespan, just like the proxy delegated to the job. However, the proxy delegated to the startd is never updated explicitly by the shadow. I think this is ok, but I don't fully understand how that proxy is used, so I need to confirm. 2011-Jan-28 15:34:53 by danb: The delegation of a proxy to the startd is for the deprecated glexec mode in which the starter is launched via glexec (GLEXEC_STARTER=true). I don't think I have introduced any new problems in this case, and since it is deprecated, I am not going to spend more time investigating.

title: Ticket #124: Perform some HDFS testing
description: Perform some HDFS testing to gain experience and confidence. Everybody focuses on testing scalability. So for the moment we will not worry so much about HDFS scalability. Instead, we will focus on availability - Can it run for days on end shuffling data? fault tolerance - What happens when block server(s) are killed/restarted? What happens when file servers are killed/restarted? What happens when block servers run out of disk space? What happens when the network dies?
remarks: 2009-Jan-30 12:53:57 by faisal: Most of these tests were conducted using JAVA API of Hadoop. The test suite uses a configurable way to generate directory and file structure with different mix of file sizes. Multiple reader and writer threads then read different files and report transfer rate. For some of the (future) tests, that directly concerns us, I will be using Hadoop's network protocol messages e.g placing all the blocks of a given file on a particular machine. Additionally, these tests mostly deals with reliability and fault-tolerance of file transfers and to some extent feature verification. We expect Hadoop to scale fairly well in terms of files, their size and number of transfers. Tests Filling up storage Once the storage is filled client will quit complaining that file could only be replicated to '0' nodes while '1' was required. Adding a new datanode server after the storage is filled to capacity Hadoop doesn't start to rebalance nodes automatically, but there are scripts to do this. In this tests HDFS started to use new node. Setting higher replication than available data nodes Didn't see any problem, HDFS will start replicating file as soon as a new data node is available. Nameserver got killed during write Transfer stopped after making couple of retires. Write call remained blocked during this time. These retires can be configured. Taking a data node offline while writing to a file Client exits after making couple of tries to reconnect to datanode server. The dead-node remained in the list of naemnode's available storage for quite some time. I saw all my attempts to write a file failing as HDFS was trying to contact the dead datanode. I will try to get more insight about this behavior from Hadoop's mailing list. Taking a datanode offline while reading a file (with no replica) Read call will be blocked and client will give up after making configurable number of retries. Taking a datanode offline while reading a file (with at-least 2 replicas) Transfer continues seamlessly. It might have an affect on performance when doing lot of parallel transfers. I might do some more tests, specially to see the performance of moving of individual blocks from one data-node to other.
creator: tannenba

title: Ticket #1111: Run DAGMan PRE and POST scripts as Condor jobs
description: Possibly have an option to run DAGMan PRE and POST scripts as actual Condor jobs (maybe in their own universe), rather than DAGMan just forking them off. The way I see this now, there would be a config knob or command-line flag to tell DAGMan to do this automatically -- it would cons up suitable submit files on the fly and do a condor_submit instead of just forking off the script. This would buy us a number of things: Machine-wide PRE/POST script throttles. Saving output of PRE/POST scripts. Generally having all of the Condor facilities to deal with PRE and POST scripts. The way I see the implementation at this point, the PRE and POST jobs would log their events to a separate log file that would not be monitored during DAGMan recovery mode. We'd still write POST script terminated events to the "real" job log, so recovery mode would work just like it does now, whether you ran the scripts as Condor jobs or not. title: Ticket #3602: RPM upgrade changes permissions, breaks privsep
description: Currently, the CHTC pool uses privsep in its HTCondor configuration (though this may change soon). The CHTC pool is also configured to use slot directories located in /var/lib/condor/execute. HTcondor will throw errors in the StarterLog, if privsep is enabled and directory ownership/mode does not reflect the following (these are the correct privsep permissions): drwxr-xr-x. 4 root root 4096 Jan 14 17:36 /var/lib/condor drwxr-xr-x. 43 root root 4096 Apr 29 17:20 /var/lib/condor/execute The error that shows up is: 04/29/13 17:09:39 privsep_reap_switchboard: error received: exited with non-zero status (1) and message (unsafe permissions in directory parent (/var/lib/condor/execute) ) 04/29/13 17:09:39 ERROR "CondorPrivSepHelper::initialize_sandbox: privsep_create_dir error on /var/lib/condor/execute/dir_53591" at line 101 in file /slots/02/dir_14487/userdir/src/condor_starter.V6.1/condor_privsep_helper.UNIX.cpp The UW HTcondor rpm sets directory ownership/mode to: drwxr-xr-x. 4 condor condor 4096 Jan 14 17:36 /var/lib/condor drwxrwxrwt. 3 condor condor 18 Jan 14 17:36 /var/lib/condor/execute/ This breaks privsep with the error seen above. It may be sensible for a newly-insalled HTCondor instance to have these ownership/modes as a default configurion; However, doing a "yum update condor" results in the the ownership/modes reverting to the default, which is privsep-incompatible. I don't really think it's good for a package to change directory ownership/mode without explicit administrator authorization, much like it's not good for a package to change configuration files without authorization. It may behoove us to alter the UW HTcondor RPM to leave directory ownership/mode alone in the case of an update. It would certainly help anybody who uses privsep (if there is anybody). This issue is probably older than 7.8.3; That's just the oldest HTcondor in the repository we use.
remarks: 2013-Apr-29 21:09:10 by nwp: Add condor to the valid-user-ids, as documented in #3573 2020-Jun-08 10:04:40 by tannenba: As privsep is deprecated, marking this ticket as abandoned.

title: Ticket #7211: Everything is Terrible, condor_now edition
description: Jaime just fixed [57671] a bug introduced in the condor_now support, where after a restart, the schedd generates match records which do not have (and never gain) a machine ad. We need to check if other parts of the condor_now support code use the machine ad for anything, and if so, how they handle it being missing. First priority is to make sure the schedd doesn't crash in those cases. Second priority is making sure that the condor_now support code (mostly in the pccc* code) doesn't leak in those cases. (I should also verify that there's garbage collection more generally, since I just don't remember.) It may be best/easiest to accomplish this by checking the match record for a machine ad as part of checking a job ID for suitability, and rejecting rather than trying to deal with it. It would be nice, if the condor_now support code does use the machine ad for something, to change it so it doesn't require it; TJ may have ideas. A substantial fraction of the pool might be inaccessible otherwise.
remarks: 2019-Aug-21 15:43:26 by tlmiller: The condor_now support code does not appear to use my_match_ad anywhere except for when trying to return the list of match records marked with now jobs. Four files in schedd.V6/ reference my_match_ad: dedicated_scheduler.cpp -- did not examine qmgmt.cpp -- only one instance of the text was to the match record member, and it was used safely. scheduler.h -- declaration schedd.cpp -- found a few place where my_match_ad was assumed to be non-NULL. 2019-Aug-21 16:29:52 by tlmiller: Jaime is more familiar with this part of the schedd than I am, so he'll take a look at the places I identified and see if any checks are actually necessary (and if so, what they should do on a failure). 2019-Aug-22 10:43:10 by jfrey: With the code as written now, I don't see a danger of dereferencing a NULL my_match_ad pointer. Once a match_rec has a non-NULL my_match_ad, the value is never set to NULL. The callers of contactStartd() and claimedStartd() also set a non-NULL my_match_ad. For swappedClaims() and CheckForClaimSwap(), the m_can_start_jobs value in match_rec guards against using a NULL my_match_ad. When making reconnect records after a restart, the dedicated scheduler queries the collector to get the slot ads for its match_rec objects. 2019-Aug-27 12:05:52 by tlmiller: I think that means we can resolve this ticket, then.

title: Ticket #5693: Recheck port exhaustion problem.
description: We were having problems around now (2016-05-26) with runs being 'interrupted' by timing out during final file transfer. The starter log shows this was caused by the starter attempting but failing to bind to an outbound port in the range of 9600-9700. This configuration only seems to have become problematic when the BaTLab upgraded to 8.4.x. When it fails to connect, it tells the shadow... which immediately reconnects, leaving no time for a port to become clear. After 8(?) retries, the shadow gives up and throws an exception. This almost immediately causes the job to be removed by the PeriodicRemove expression, since the job will be idle and have started more than once (and since we want to our retries at the DAG level because Metronome otherwise gets /horribly/ confused, we don't let that happen). It's unclear if 8.2.x didn't have a port exhaustion problem for some reason, or if it just handled file transfer connection failures differently enough to recover, and so we never noticed.

title: Ticket #5739: metaknobs should have arguments
description: It is awkward if not impossible to use config metaknobs to help configure a collector tree or HAD. Both of these would be cleaner and easier if metaknobs had support for argument passing. So you could do something like this config file fragment use FEATURE : CollectorNode(2, 9702), CollectorNode(3, 9703) And it would expand to this expansion of the above config COLLECTOR2 = $(COLLECTOR) COLLECTOR2_ARGS = -f -local-name COLLECTOR2 -p 9702 COLLECTOR2.COLLECTOR_LOG = $(LOG)/Collector2Log DAEMON_LIST = $(DAEMON_LIST) COLLECTOR2 COLLECTOR3 = $(COLLECTOR) COLLECTOR3_ARGS = -f -local-name COLLECTOR3 -p 9703 COLLECTOR3.COLLECTOR_LOG = $(LOG)/Collector3Log DAEMON_LIST = $(DAEMON_LIST) COLLECTOR3 When the metaknob $FEATURE.CollectorNode is defined as $FEATURE.CollectorNode COLLECTOR$(1) = $(COLLECTOR) if $(2?) COLLECTOR$(1)_ARGS = -f -local-name COLLECTOR$(1) -p $(2) else COLLECTOR$(1)_ARGS = -f -local-name COLLECTOR$(1) -sock collector$(1) endif COLLECTOR$(1).COLLECTOR_LOG = $(LOG)/Collector$(1)Log DAEMON_LIST = $(DAEMON_LIST) COLLECTOR$(1) Metaknob arguments will be optional, if the metaknob name is followed by (), then the value in side of the () will be split on , and stripped of leading and trailing whitespace, and then substituted for $(0), $(1), $(2), etc in the value of the metaknob before it is parsed into config statements. In metaknob statements any $(arg) will be substituted if arg starts with a digit (since that cannot be a valid param name). The substitutions shall be $(0) all of the args $(0?) 1 if any arguments, 0 if no arguments $(0#) the number of arguments (i.e. the number of commas+1) $(1) the first argument $(1?) 1 if the first argument is non-empty, 0 if it is empty $(1+) all of the arguments, starting with the first one. equivalent to $(0) $(2) the second argument $(2?) 1 if the second argument is non-empty, 0 if it is empty $(2+) all of the arguments, starting with the second one $(3) the third argument etc

title: Ticket #1280: Gram jobmanager version command doesn't work in most cases
description: Gram's jobmanager version command doesn't work in most cases. The gram client library explicitly disables proxy delegation for this command. This causes the jobmanager to fail on start-up when it attempts to acquire a proxy (as it wants the delegated one). This causes the jobmanager to close the connection to the client without sending a reply. This results in a gram error 10 being returned to the caller. All versions of the jobmanager do this, so the client can't even determine if the jobmanager is GRAM2 or GRAM5. If the server has a proxy for the mapped user in the default location in /tmp, the jobmanager is able to start up properly and either send back a valid reply (GRAM5) or an error 91 (GRAM2). This will normally not happen. A simple fix would be to allow delegation of the proxy for the version command. The change would have to be made inside the gram client library. If a fix isn't available from Globus in time for 7.5.2, we should patch the version of Globus we build for Condor to include this change. More information is available here: http://jira.globus.org/browse/GRAM-141
remarks: 2010-Apr-12 11:04:43 by jfrey: If the version command returns gram error 10, the gridmanager assumes the server is GRAM5, which will often be a wrong assumption. 2010-Apr-13 09:43:15 by jfrey: Update Globus external to 5.0.1, which fixes this problem. Change committed to V7_5_2-branch.

title: Ticket #3747: DMTCP checkpoints can't handle being moved
description: The problem appears to be that when DMTCP restarts after a checkpoint, the next time it checkpoints it really want to write a checkpoint file (ckpt_BINNAME_CLUSTER_PROC_HEX-PID-HEX.dmtcp) into the old checkpoint location. Other files involved in the checkpoint are written the new directory. If you're on a single computer, running as yourself, this works fine as you probably didn't move the directory. It even works if you move the directory because DMTCP will helpfully re-create the directory if necessary. But under HTCondor running as another user (the usual "run as root/condor" configuration), you're doomed, because your job runs in a directory named $EXECUTE/dir_$PID, which (usually) changes when your job restarts. DMTCP will try to recreate the directory, but assuming a typical configuration will be blocked by permissions. DMTCP will exit with 99. DMTCP is supposed to handle changed directories through the DMTCP_RESTART_DIR environment variable or the --restartdir/-d option to dmtcp_restart_script.sh. I tracked this down with DMTCP 1.2.6. The current release is 1.2.7. (I moved back earlier trying to see if there was a regression.) Reported to the DMTCP developers on June 11, 2013. They replied hoping the head of SVN was fixed, but we needed to use the --ckptdir option or the DMTCP_CHECKPOINT_DIR environment variable set to ./ Testing... Possible fix/workaround: #3749: Use filesystem namespaces to present non-changing execute directory

title: Ticket #1900: Running jobs leave queue when held
description: The code to start using the new TRANSFERRING_OUTPUT job status (#1641) introduced a bug. If a running vanilla, java, or vm universe job is held (e.g. via condor_hold), it ends up being removed instead. When the starter informs the shadow that the job is no longer running, the shadow always changes the job's status to TRANSFERRING_OUTPUT, regardless of whether the job was killed or exited on its own. When the shadow exits, this causes the schedd to remove the job. The quickest fix is to stop using the TRANSFERRING_OUTPUT status for now, since nothing relies on it yet. When we want to reintroduce its use, either the shadow needs to be much more careful about when it changes the job status to TRANSFERRING_OUTPUT or the schedd should change the status as a result of the shadow exiting. In the latter case, the TRANSFERRING_OUTPUT status would only be used when delayed output transfer is in use (i.e. start a new job immediately and transfer output in parallel).

title: Ticket #6396: noop_job in submit isn't honored by schedd when a claim is reused
description: For reference: submit value noop_job is translated to IsNoopJob in the job ad. When the schedd sees a job with IsNoopJob==True, it marks it as completed and goes on its merry way. However, it does this in count_a_job(), which works for most jobs, but is not sufficient for all jobs. Particularly, when reusing a claim, it is possible to have a noop job that count_a_job() has not yet processed (because it was recently submitted), so the schedd goes ahead and executes the job as if this attribute were not present. We need to check for the IsNoopJob attribute when searching for a runnable job. For efficient processing of IsNoopJob, we should also be checking just after the job is submitted. Now the way the schedd finds jobs to run when it gets match records is to walk the PrioRec array checking each job in order. this guarantees that the highest priority matching job gets the match. In 8.6.6 and earlier versions of the schedd. noop jobs are put into the PrioRec array, so FindRunnableJob finds them. If they were skipped when building the PrioRec array, then they would not be run, although because the IsNoopJob is an expression, it should still be checked in Runnable to insure that even if a job ends up in the PrioRec array, it will not be run.
remarks: 2017-Sep-06 17:03:17 by zmiller: To reproduce, open attachment and submit a.dag, let it run to completion. When the bug is present, jobs N3 and N4 will execute even though they are marked noop, and you'll see result files output.N2, output.N3, and output.N4. If the bug is fixed, you should see only output.N2. (run clean in between trials to remove output, logs, dagman cruft.) 2017-Sep-07 11:21:09 by johnkn: One way to avoid hitting this bug is to make sure that the noop jobs don't match any resources. This can be accomplished by setting requirements=false as well as noop_job=true to the submit file. 2017-Sep-07 12:47:11 by johnkn: The fix (for stable) will be to skip the noop jobs when building the PrioRec array, and ALSO to check for noop jobs in Runnable. This will prevent jobs that were submitted as noop jobs from being found when searching for runnable jobs, and also prevent them from being run if the IsNoopJob expression changes to true after the PrioRec array is built, but before the job is actually started. 2017-Oct-26 14:54:21 by zmiller: CODE REVIEW: Looks good. 2017-Oct-27 14:58:31 by tim: Doc Review: Complete

title: Ticket #1453: Documentation required for new SCHEDD_CLUSTER_MAXIMUM_VALUE
description: Need to update documentation to include description of new configuration parameter SCHEDD_CLUSTER_MAXIMUM_VALUE. See also #1315
remarks: 2010-Jun-14 13:56:48 by eje: ====================================== SCHEDD_CLUSTER_MAXIMUM_VALUE is an upper bound on the job cluster id. If this parameter is set to a value (M), the maximum job cluster id assigned to any job will be (M-1). When the maximum id is reached, job ids will wrap around back to SCHEDD_CLUSTER_INITIAL_VALUE. The default value is zero, in which case behavior is no maximum cluster id (backward compatible). Caveat: If you set this parameter to a value (M), you are responsible for ensuring that you have fewer than (M) jobs in your que at any time. Otherwise, in the event that many new jobs are queued up simultaneously, it is possible for jobs to be erroneously assigned duplicate cluster ids, which will result in a corrupted job queue. See also: SCHEDD_CLUSTER_INITIAL_VALUE, SCHEDD_CLUSTER_INCREMENT_VALUE ===================================== Actually, the true caveat is a bit stronger than that: user is responsible for making sure that old jobs complete before new job ids wrap around. In other words, if you have a really long-running job with id (x.0), and cluster id wraps back around to (x), you'll have a problem, even if cluster (x+1, x+2, ...) are free. Here is some content for initial-val and increment-val: ================================ SCHEDD_CLUSTER_INITIAL_VALUE specifies the first cluster id number that will be assigned. This parameter defaults to 1. If the job cluster id reaches the value set by SCHEDD_CLUSTER_MAXIMUM_VALUE and wraps, it will be re-set to SCHEDD_CLUSTER_INITIAL_VALUE. Note that the most recently used cluster id is saved, and persists across shutdown and restart. If the "job_queue.log" file is removed, then after system restart cluster ids will be assigned starting from SCHEDD_CLUSTER_INITIAL_VALUE. See also: SCHEDD_CLUSTER_INCREMENT_VALUE, SCHEDD_CLUSTER_MAXIMUM_VALUE ================================ ================================ SCHEDD_CLUSTER_INCREMENT_VALUE specifies the increment used to assign new cluster id numbers. Its default value is 1. For example, if SCHEDD_CLUSTER_INITIAL_VALUE is set to 2, and SCHEDD_CLUSTER_INCREMENT_VALUE is set to 2, then cluster id numbers will be {2, 4, 6, ...} See also: SCHEDD_CLUSTER_INITIAL_VALUE, SCHEDD_CLUSTER_MAXIMUM_VALUE ================================ 2010-Oct-20 16:03:30 by jfrey: Bulk change of target version from v070504 to v070505 using ./ticket-target-mover. 2011-Jan-27 14:46:04 by danb: Bulk change of target version from v070505 to v070506 using ./ticket-target-mover. 2011-Feb-01 16:08:44 by tannenba: Bulk change of target version from v070506 to NULL using ./ticket-target-mover. 2011-Jun-29 11:36:04 by smoler: This ticket was mostly finished long ago. title: Ticket #3481: Different "idle time" counts for partitionable slots than normal slots
description: In glideinWMS, we have a DAEMON_SHUTDOWN expression that essentially does: (TotalTimeUnclaimedIdle < T1) || (TotalTimeClaimedBusy =!= Undefined && TotalTimeUnclaimedIdle < T2) This works fine for non-partitionable slots. For partitionable slots, the parent slot always remains in the Idle state, no matter the state of the child slots, so this metric doesn't work. We can hack around it to come up with something usable, but we can't replicate non-partitionable DAEMON_SHUTDOWN behavior with partitionable slots. Something analogous to TotalTimeUnclaimedIdle may work, but it needs to start counting only when the parent reclaims all the child slot resources (so the entire slot is truly "idle"). We'd also want some parameter to let us know if the parent slot has ever created child slots (analogous to TotalTimeClaimedBusy being defined or not).
remarks: 2013-Sep-24 17:14:09 by danb: It does still seem useful to have aggregate metrics for slot usage in the startd, but it seems to me the behavior you want is nearly achievable, given the new attributes added in #3712. For detecting if the parent slot has ever created a child slot, one could use TotalJobStarts. There is also TotalRecentJobStarts which is the number of jobs started in the past 20 minutes. One could use that in the DAEMON_SHUTDOWN expression like this: TotalSlots == 1 && TotalRecentJobStarts == 0 && CurrentTime-DaemonStartTime > T1 One problem is a race condition between the time one long-running job ends and the next one begins. During that time, the above expression could become true. The race might be solved if we had TotalRecentJobCompletions instead, assuming it is updated before the expression is evaluated. 2013-Sep-25 14:37:05 by burt: We could implement it this way, but it makes some of the glideinWMS termination knobs useless if T1 or T2 are greater than 20 minutes. (Typical values are shorter). Would it make sense if EnteredCurrentState was reset when the parent slot allocated or deallocated child slots? title: Ticket #6379: Job cluster completion and progress notification
description: Note that notifications from Dagman are beyond the scope of this ticket. This ticket is about notifications implemented in the Schedd. Email notification on completion of a single job is fairly useless in a world where users are running hundreds or even tens of thousands of jobs - what is need is notifications that work at the cluster level or even at the batch level. Some expected use cases I want to know when all of my jobs have completed (i.e. left the queue). I want to know when my job has started running. (i.e. high memory jobs) I want to know if any, all, or some number of my jobs go on hold I want to know when my jobs is no longer making progress (i.e. either finished, or on hold, or the dag/materialization factory has been paused) I want periodic (daily?) updates on the progress of my jobs. The current design for notification consists of two statements in the submit file. notification = NEVER|COMPLETE|ERROR|ALWAYS notify_user = <email_or_username> These attributes are checked on each shadow exit, and an email is either sent or not based on the shadow exit code and the notification value. I propose to "embrace and extend" this mechanism by redefining the notification mechanism so it is triggered by CLUSTER removal rather than shadow exit, and/or by periodic expression evaluation. The user interface for this will be 2 new submit statements and 4 new options for the notification keyword. notification = NEVER|COMPLETE|ERROR|ALWAYS|START|HOLD|PERIODIC|STUCK notification_requirements = <expr> notification_rate = <number>[<units>] notify_user = <email_or_username> This would have the effect of changing the notification for multi-proc jobs from one per job to one for all of the jobs. This is a better fit for all of the use cases listed above. There will be a SCHEDD knob to allow the old per-proc notification behavior, and a new job attribute that must be set in order for a user to opt in to the old per-proc notification behavior on schedds that allow it. Multiple values will be allowed for the notification keyword in the submit file, for instance this: notification = start,complete,stuck would result in notifications being sent when the first job starts, when the cluster is no longer capable of making progress or when the jobs are all complete. There will be two trigger points in the schedd for the new notification behavior for multi-proc jobs (single proc jobs will still use the shadow for notifications) When the cluster object is removed, a final notification may be sent. Periodically, (5 minute intervals?) an expression will be evaluated against the cluster object, when it triggers - and if the previous notification was not too recent, it will send a notification. Attributes will be added to a special ad created for purposes of evaluation of the notification trigger expression. These attributes will contain counts of jobs in various states. The ad will be created on the fly and not stored in the job queue, (so it will not end up being written to the history file in each of the jobs.) Notifications will be edge triggered, so for instance, notification=HOLD will send a notification the first time a job goes on hold, not each time. Notifications can also be triggered by complex conditions, and will be rate limited. so it will be possible to request a notification when more than 10% of jobs go on hold, or to get a status email once a day.
remarks: 2017-Dec-20 13:17:06 by tannenba: LIGO requests that we think about how this functionality may (or may not) work with respect to DAG workflows. Could the proposed mechanism be tweaked to enable DAG users to reap the benefits ? 2017-Dec-22 13:39:24 by tpdownes: How flexible do you intend periodic expression notification to be? For example, it is your intent that I could setup a rule that said "hey, I noticed your job is using X but you requested Y"? Where X is either well below or well above Y and could be CPU, Memory, etc. 2018-Oct-17 13:06:44 by johnkn: It was not my intent that PERIODIC these notifications have the ability to change the state of any jobs. The intent here is to report on progress - so the PERIODIC notifications would indicate number of jobs in each state. In particular, the expressions would probably not have access to any specific job attributes - only aggregates would be available.

title: Ticket #1516: new ClassAds don't support semicolon as function argument separator
description: In old ClassAds, arguments to a function can be separated with commas or semicolons. In new ClassAds, only commas can be used. In old ClassAds, the use of semicolons is an older syntax that is now avoided, but still valid. We've identified two users of Condor who use the semicolon notation. They are the Swift workload management system (https://svn.ci.uchicago.edu/svn/vdl2/usertools/swift/osgedu-list-sites) and the ReSS service of OSG. As such, we should make new ClassAds recognize this notation when in old ClassAd compatibility mode (i.e. when _useOldClassAdSemantics is set to true).

title: Ticket #6729: memory leak in submitMany python binding
description: FNAL reports that the submitMany python binding is leaking memory. Their own ticket for this is https://github.com/dmwm/WMCore/issues/8493. This ticket indicates the problem is with 8.5.7, but we have email from them indicating that the problem reproduces on 8.6.11 and 8.7.7. remarks: 2018-Aug-01 17:29:36 by tannenba: Possible workaround: Using submitMany() is a pain in the rear. It is a lot easier to to submit jobs via the htcondor.Submit() object, and (hopefully!) this does not suffer the memory leak bug. htcondor.Submit() uses the same key/value pairs that you would use in a regular condor_submit file, so no need to come up with a classad for the job. Example of submitting a 100 jobs (procs) into one cluster : import htcondor sub = htcondor.Submit() # Specify executable sub['Executable']='Example.exe' # Specify a custom attribute - use the '+' just like a submit file sub['+MyCustomAttribute']='True' # Specify arguments, using $(Process) like a submit file sub['Arguments']='-run_number $(Process)' # Send 100 jobs into a cluster with schedd.transaction() as txn: sub.queue(txn,100) 2018-Aug-07 10:45:54 by johnkn: I did some investigation, it's leaking the classAds that are returned by submitMany via the 4th argument. But only if you don't supply the 4th argument. Not really sure why this is so, but you can easily work around the bug just by calling submitMany with 4 arguments like this: submitMany(clusterAd, procAds, 0, []) 2018-Aug-07 13:43:23 by johnkn: actually schedd.submitMany(clusterAd, procAds, 0, None) Is better, because None causes the creation of the result_ads to be skipped entirely. 2018-Oct-08 15:13:19 by tlmiller: Code Review Although it doesn't show up in the commit, in submitMany() we explicitly check for and handle the case that ad_results is not a list. submit() turns around and calls submitMany() without even looking at ad_results, so that should be fine, too. Approved. Documentation looks good as well.

title: Ticket #5555: Broken LOWPORT/HIGHPORT on Windows.
description: In Sock::bindWithin(), when we compute the (semi-random) offset into the port range, it's possible for there to be integer overflow, now that we're no longer taking the pseudorandom value mod 1000000. If overflow occurs, the offset can be negative, and since the initial bind() on Windows (basically) always succeeds (see #4711), we won't notice. The obvious solution is to add the mod 1000000 back in, but the function could really use a rewrite to (a) do all of its math in unsigned shorts and (b) use one of the util lib's random number generators rather than trying to roll its own. A PRNG would probably be better in terms of avoiding duplicate initial port numbers anyway, since we don't have to worry about sampling errors. Ben Cotton's customer wants this fix before the end of April, when they'd like to go into production.
remarks: 2016-Mar-10 13:52:03 by johnkn: the fix for #5375 used a signed quantity for the random value, which would allow the the value to go below LOWPORT on windows. (linux uses a random value < 1million, but windows random value is a full 32 bit int). 2016-Mar-10 13:57:15 by tannenba: Can someone explain why the code doesn't simply call get_random_uint() from the util lib instead of these bizarre platform dependent attempts to generate a random number? 2016-Mar-22 15:10:47 by tlmiller: Code Review Approved. Hopefully more-accurately than last time.

title: Ticket #4850: Collector ad is dropped for personal HTCondor
description: Ever since we added COLLECTOR_USES_SHARED_PORT, the collector does not listen on a UDP port for personal HTCondor installs (which use arbitrary ports) if USE_SHARED_PORT=true. This is because, when shared port is in use and there's no specific port requested, no additional UDP/TCP socket pair is requested. It's assumed, in this case, the only way to find a daemon is through a collector or $COLLECTOR_ADDRESS_FILE. It works in all cases except for updating collector ads - which forcibly disable TCP updates. In the case of a UPDATE_COLLECTOR_AD, we should check if the sinful has noUDP and act accordingly: Allow TCP updates if this is not a daemon Allow TCP updates if we are not updating our own command socket Otherwise, utilize the fact we always have a UDP port for the super-user socket - send the update through that!

title: Ticket #4153: add relro and PIE to build for improved security hardening
description: From security policy description: Partial relro is when you have -Wl,-z,relro in the LDFLAGS for building libraries. Partial relro means that some ELF sections are reordered so that overflows in some likely sections don't affect others and the local offset table is readonly. To get full relro, you also need to have: -Wl,-z,bind_now (or -Wl,-z,now) added to LDFLAGS. What this does is make the Global Offset table and Procedure Lookup Table readonly. This takes some time, so its only worth it for apps that have a real possibility of being attacked. This would be setuid/setgid/setcap and daemons. There are some security critical apps that can have this too. If the apps likely parses files from an untrusted source (internet), then it might also want to have full relro. To enable PIE, you would pass -fPIE -DPIE in the CFLAGS and -pie in the LDFLAGS. What PIE does is randomize the locations of important items such as the base address of an executable and position of libraries, heap, and stack, in a process's address space. Sometimes this is called ASLR. Its designed to make buffer/heap overflow, return into libc attacks much harder. Part of the way it does this is to make a new section in the ELF image that is writable to redirect function calls to the correct address (offsets). This has to be writable because each invocation will have different layouts and needs to be fixed up. So, when you have an application with PIE, you want full relro so that these sections become readonly and not part of an attacker's target areas.

title: Ticket #1644: machine invalidation ads match ads from all machines
description: I now understand what is causing the CMS glideinWMS machine ads to get invalidated unexpectedly. The collector is 7.4. The startds are a mix of 7.4 and 7.5. The problem is that the collector is receiving ads from 7.5 startds, which insert some extra attributes into the invalidation request. Those extra attributes are used by the 7.5 collector to do the invalidation more efficiently (hash-table lookup rather than query evaluation). The 7.4 collector does the old inefficient method of evaluating a query against all ads to see which ads to invalidate. It is supposed to ignore the extra attributes. Unfortunately, the extra attributes unintentionally change the meaning of the query so that it matches all ads! Observe: 09/06 14:48:00 Got INVALIDATE_STARTD_ADS 09/06 14:48:00 **** Removing invalidated ad: "< glidein_2180@node200 , 172.16.1.200 >" 09/06 14:48:00 **** Removing invalidated ad: "< glidein_32077@node156 , 172.16.1.156 >" 09/06 14:48:00 **** Removing invalidated ad: "< glidein_19637@sbgwn91.in2p3.fr , 193.48.85.141 >" 09/06 14:48:00 **** Removing invalidated ad: "< glidein_29548@farm012.ts.infn.it , 140.105.222.82 >" 09/06 14:48:00 **** Removing invalidated ad: "< glidein_5254@wn-a3-09.brunel.ac.uk , 172.30.1.151 >" 09/06 14:48:00 **** Removing invalidated ad: "< glidein_9936@wn-b1-06.brunel.ac.uk , 172.30.1.183 >" 09/06 14:48:00 **** Removing invalidated ad: "< glidein_23569@polgrid130.in2p3.fr , 134.158.132.30 >" 09/06 14:48:00 **** Removing invalidated ad: "< glidein_30735@grid-wn0849.desy.de , 131.169.162.192 >" 09/06 14:48:00 **** Removing invalidated ad: "< glidein_16706@cabinet-4-4-13.t2.ucsd.edu , 169.228.131.93 >" 09/06 14:48:00 **** Removing invalidated ad: "< glidein_17988@cabinet-3-3-0.t2.ucsd.edu , 169.228.131.143 >" 09/06 14:48:00 **** Removing invalidated ad: "< glidein_14761@cabinet-7-7-31.t2.ucsd.edu , 169.228.130.187 >" 09/06 14:48:00 (Invalidated 11 ads) 09/06 14:48:00 The invalidation query was this: MyType = "Query" TargetType = "Machine" UpdateSequenceNumber = 0 Name = "glidein_15000@wn182.lcg.cscs.ch" Requirements = (Name == "glidein_15000@wn182.lcg.cscs.ch") DaemonStartTime = 1283808198 MyAddress = "<148.187.66.182:45970?CCBID=169.228.130.23:9677#751>" See how the Requirements refers to Name? That is intended to refer to the Name attribute in the machine ad, but instead it refers to the Name attribute in the invalidation query! How to Fix The startd needs to be fixed to specify target scope explicitly in the query. However, there is still the problem of what to do about 7.5.3 startds that generate the dangerous invalidation queries. Perhaps if attributes for generating a hash key are present, we should never evaluate the query, even if no ad is found with a matching hash key. Then the question is whether the 7.4 collector needs to be patched as well. I'm waiting to hear whether CMS is willing to upgrade to a 7.5 collector or not.
remarks: 2010-Sep-07 16:00:11 by danb: It turns out that #1579 intentionally removed explicit TARGET scoping in the invalidation queries and made the 7.5 collector force TARGET scope when evaluating such queries. So it was really a combination of #1579 and #1316 that caused the compatibility problem with 7.4. After discussing with Jaime, we agreed that TARGET scope should be added back to the invalidation queries. The longer-term goal of getting rid of TARGET rewriting can still be achieved by getting rid of the invalidation query altogether. Instead, we should always send enough information to build a hash key for the ad to be invalidated. It may be useful for admins to have a way to invalidate multiple ads via a constraint, but this should probably just be a separate command (maybe ADMINISTRATOR-level). 2010-Sep-07 17:27:39 by danb: I have created patches for 7.5 that address the problem. Also, #1342 has been resolved so that we can eventually phase out the use an invalidation query expression by Condor daemons. I am closing this ticket. If it turns out that somebody has a pressing need for a 7.4 patch, we will have to revisit the issue.
