title: Ticket #444: Increasing DAGMan throughput with condor_submit
description: If DAGMan has 1000 ready nodes and is told it may submit all of them, then it will do one submit per ready node. It would be much nicer if dagman could collect all of the submit files, concatenate them in memory, then blast them all to the schedd in one condor_submit using its stdin as a pipe. There would still just be one cluster node per dag node in this model, it would just increase the throughput of the jobs submitted into Condor. It would seem that a new feature would have to be added to condor_submit's parsing of its submit file, that of the keyword "newcluster" which would reset everything back to default for a new cluster to be described after the keyword. Multiple uses of the keyword may appear. A small performance test needs to be written to see if 100,000 jobs submitted individually, or 100,000 jobs in one submit file submitted with one condor_q would be faster. If faster, this ticket should stay, if equal or slower, then this ticket should be abandoned as it won't increase throughput. Things in dagman that would have to change would be the condor_submit parsing code, and the submission code for the ready node list.
remarks: 2009-Apr-30 16:08:05 by psilord: After having a conversation with Dan about it, this is what he had to say: (16:00:13) Peter Keller: Hey, if I submitted 100,000 clusters into Condor with individual submits, or with a gigantic file and one submit, which do you think would be faster? After both submits the job ad information would be identical in the schedd. (16:01:12) Dan Bradley: I think the individual submit file would be faster. (16:01:21) Dan Bradley: But not by much (16:01:46) Peter Keller: What do you think is the limiting factor? (16:04:22) Dan Bradley: In my recent submit speed tests, I found that the time it takes for submit to initialize itself (reading config etc.) has a cost. Running 5 submit loops in parallel is faster. Behond that, there's not much gain. (16:04:54) Dan Bradley: The peak submit rate (with ~5 submit loops) is about 30% higher than with a single submit loop. (16:05:15) Dan Bradley: Therefore, I'd guess about the same performance difference for a single submit vs. a submit loop. (16:05:29) Peter Keller: Interesting. Thanks! So, initially, maybe this wouldn't buy us anything. Someone would have to look closely at Dan's submit speed tests and see if an advantage would be had.

The short version is that I'm undoing this change.

title: Ticket #5062: Blahp purge_interval causes CE to lose track of LSF jobs
description: Wei at SLAC has an issue when he is using the BLParser to manage his LSF jobs where a too low purge interval removes jobs from the job registry (causing HTCondor CE to lose track of the LSF job) and a too high purge interval causes CE jobs to start tracking the incorrect job (his LSF job ID's are recycled on the order of a few days). Can we find a Goldilocks purge_interval time for Wei or perhaps there's another solution?
remarks: 2015-Jun-17 15:55:05 by tannenba: Francesco, are you able to give Jaime a helping hand with this issue? Thanks 2015-Jun-19 09:10:28 by Francesco.Prelz: We discussed about this issue at Condor Week, I believe. As the LSF job id is currently the only key that identifies a job (both in LSF and in BLAH), we can think of adding a new job state that allows old BLAH job registry entries to be safely ignored when the initial (job submit) registration of a new job with the same ID is received. However, unless job_registry_use_mmap is set to 'true', checking for the existance of old entries can slow down job submission enough to get complaints (we got a few tickets from CERN on this a while ago), so this duplicate ID check feature would either have to be optional (with a config knob) or just be applied when job_registry_use_mmap is true. In case this way to address the issue is acceptable, what is the desired time frame ? I should have some time to handle this myself on July 1-3. If it's too late I need to volunteer one of my colleagues. 2015-Sep-08 16:00:59 by blin: I've attached a patch from Brian Bockelman that prevents the purging of running/idle/held jobs. It got lost in chat a ways back but perhaps this is a solution worth entertaining? 2015-Sep-09 15:19:09 by tannenba: Francesco, we are at a point now where we really need a BLAHP patch as this bug is causing active pain in OSG. Would you be able to have a patch posted to this ticket by September 23, 2015? (aka two weeks from now) Please let us know either way. Thanks! 2015-Sep-11 07:15:13 by Francesco.Prelz: Ok, now I know the time frame... I almost finished moving my apartment. I'll be at CERN on Sep 14-16 but I should be able to attach a patch by the 23rd. 2015-Sep-11 07:18:43 by Francesco.Prelz: BTW: regardimg my earlier remark on this ticket. Is job_registry_use_mmap set to true or false on typical OSG configurations ? 2015-Sep-11 09:47:22 by blin: It defaults to 'no' in the blahp that the OSG ships. 2015-Sep-11 11:28:28 by Francesco.Prelz: After running through the involved code, keeping into account that you don't use mmap to access the BLAH index plus the fact our other customer had us remove all job ID uniqueness checks for better efficiency, I'd first of all try the very simple patch I posted here: http://www.mi.infn.it/~prelz/job_registry.patch. I ran through many cases and unless I missed something it should be all that's needed to make sure that old jobs with duplicate IDs are effectively ignored for status updates, queries and job control without losing information and with no additional operations. Your case shows that this makes sense in general. Please let us know how it goes and sorry for not turning around to this earlier. 2015-Sep-16 13:25:49 by blin: Thanks Francesco, I'll get this to the customer so they can test out if the fix works for them. 2015-Sep-18 11:27:42 by blin: Francesco, out of curiousity, is this the job ID uniqueness patch you were speaking about? https://github.com/prelz/BLAH/commit/e61b123b8399290ee622a00f02234670eb99b3aa 2015-Sep-21 04:01:04 by Francesco.Prelz: That patch would ensure job ID uniqueness only for BLAH sending jobs into Condor. What I was referring to was a way to add a specific status bit for jobs with duplicate IDs in the BLAH registry so that they can be ignored. After some pondering over the code I concluded that would add a significant inefficiency when inserting new jobs -and- should not be needed by anyone, as the database is always queried by ID via the job_registry_get_recnum(), so we can set the preference for more recent jobs where duplicate keys are found there. 2015-Sep-21 15:27:33 by blin: So what happens to the older job when duplicate keys are found? Are they no longer tracked in the job registry? 2015-Sep-22 04:01:14 by Francesco.Prelz: They are still there and they will be found if you iterate over all jobs or if you index the registry on a key that is truly unique (CREAM for instance uses its own unique prefix), but for status updates and lookups based on the batch job ID or the BLAH job ID (currently just a prefix tacked onto the batch job ID) the older job will be hidden by the newer one and effectively forgotten.

title: Ticket #852: Shadow and local starter may skip final job ad update to sched
description: Both the shadow and the starter (for local universe) use the QmgrJobUpdater class to forward job ad updates to the schedd. QmgrJobUpdater contains an optimization that skips the final update to the schedd if there's no history file. The theory is that if the job ad is about to be removed from the queue and won't be saved anywhere, we can save some of the schedd's time. This ignores a number of cases where the job ad doesn't disappear into the ether on completion or removal: LeaveJobInQueue = True Quill PER_JOB_HISTORY_DIR Rather than try to check for these cases and any future ones, QmgrJobUpdater should always do the final update.

title: Ticket #5127: make condor_userprio -long output easier to process
description: The userprio ad that is returned from the negotiator is very hard to work with because it's one big ad that is logically multiple ads where attributes that end in a common integer refer to the same group/user information. For instance, if there a two users, the ad might look like this Name1 = "foo" Priority1 = 10 Name2 = "bar" Priority2 = 12 And would be processed by condor_userprio as if it were really this Id = 1 Name = "foo" Priority = 10 Id = 2 Name = "bar" Priority = 12 We should change the negotiator to return the second form rather than the first, but in the mean time (and for backward compatibility). The usefulness of condor_userprio -long could be enhanced by having it convert from the first form to the second on the fly. This would allow the addition of -af and -constraint arguments in condor_userprio.
remarks: 2015-Jul-02 09:36:43 by johnkn: This commit adds arguments -legacy and -modular as modifiers to -long. also -autoformat (-af) which implies -modular. -legacy forces the old form of -long, which is one ad for all userprio information with attribute names having an integer appended to indicate which record. -modular is the improved form, where there is one ad per record. -af operates on, (and therefore forces) the modular form. in the modular form, the first ad contains only 2 attributes: NumSubmittors = 23 LastUpdate = 1435304615 NumSubmittors indicates how many subsequent ads there will be, these ads will be either group records or submittor records. In the current implementation, the group records will be first, followed by the submittor records with the <none> group being the first group. Groups have these attributes. title: Ticket #3159: condor_config.generic should only contain macros
description: The condor_config.generic file that gets installed, typically in /etc/condor/condor_config, contains many parameters, $ grep -v -e "^[ ]*#" -e "^$" /etc/condor/condor_config | wc -l -> 313 (not all 313 are params, some are macros, about 300 are unique) Some params should simply be removed, e.g. HDFS values do not work OOTB. Params without defaults in the param table should be added to the param table. Then, The params with defaults in the param table should be removed. title: Ticket #501: Turn the Condor static libraries on Windows into DLLs
description: After the upgrade from VS6 to VS2K8 the Condor executables for Windows almost doubled in size and have increased their memory footprint. It is likely that we can decrease both these sizes by converting all of the Condor static libraries into DLLs. Milestones 1. Decorate library source code [For Z] Create a new branch from the master; For each library, identify each symbol it "exports" (i.e. other libraries, tools use) and decorate them accordingly; For decoration styles, see the "Decoration Samples" subsection bellow. 2. Create new dynamic link library targets Have the Visual Studio Project files create DLLs instead of static libraries from the current library code. 3. Refractor libraries Not all library code is used in every tool, so there may be a way to save even more runtime space by making smaller cousins to the existing libraries that cater to very specialized needs, like, for example, security. Decoration Samples Linux Decoration Samples http://people.redhat.com/drepper/dsohowto.pdf Windows Decoration Samples /** DLL import/export definitions. */ #ifdef CONDOR_DLL #define CONDOR_API __declspec(dllexport) #define CONDOR_INSTANTIATE #else #define CONDOR_API __declspec(dllimport) #define CONDOR_INSTANTIATE export #endif /** A sample class. */ class CONDOR_API Daemon { public: Daemon (); }; /** A sample template. */ template<class T> class CONDOR_API Vector { public: Vector (); size_t Length () const; /** ... */ }; /** A sample template instance. This does not create an object. It only forces the generation of all of the members of the class. It exports them from the DLL and imports them into the executable file. Ugly, I know. */ CONDOR_INSTANTIATE template class CONDOR_API Vector<int>; /** A sample basic symbol (can be any type). */ extern CONDOR_API int n; /** A sample function. */ CONDOR_API int f ( int x ); I though about adding CONDOR_CLASS but I thought that maybe that was too cute. Linux and UNIX systems will need to define CONDOR_API and CONDOR_INSTANTIATE as nothing, to avoid any compiler errors. The above defines are to be included in the Windows only Condor system header file.
remarks: 2009-May-25 09:05:34 by tannenba: The conversion of static libs into dynamic libraries would be useful on more than just Win32 imho. All the benefits you talk about would be welcome on Linux etc as well. Also, imho I am not certain there is much benefit to having a while pile of shared libs. What benefit is there to having a util lib, c++ util lib, cedar lib, dc lib, qmgmt lib, etc, etc? Since practically all Condor binaries want to link w/ all libs anyhow, and since ClassAds is really the only library of interest outside of Condor, perhaps we should just have libclassads and one big libcondor.[so|dll] and be done with it. 2009-Jul-10 21:09:19 by burnett: I'd like to see a few separate ones to begin with. Not all the tools depend on all the libraries, so it would be a pity to strap on that extra baggage. Second, once they are converted, I'd like to look at how they should be combined or further separated (if necessary). It seems reasonable right now to combine condor_util and cpp_util, but most tool/daemons use very little of each library all at once (well, the cpp library anyway). Maybe it makes sense to divvy up the cpp library in to meaningful modules... unless we cannot justify the time... which I think we can, if we can slim down the starters, shadows and make sure that a Windows CM can actually scale to some respectable size (even if it still does not compete with the Linux one). 2009-Jul-17 14:00:16 by burnett: Bellow is response from a newsgroup. Most of the information we already know, but I'm just posting it so that we have an explicit record, in case someone who does not know all the details is reading this. "Ben Burnett" wrote: > Has anyone converted a large number of static libraries to DLLs using an automated method (or semi-automated)? I'm not sure it is possible to do it automatically unless you have highly sofisticated parser tool which can patch the files according to predefined rules. In order to make a DLL from LIB you need to do the following steps: 1. Go through all headers and add calling convention and __declspec(dllimport/dllexport) modifiers for each function declaration. You can spare __declspec(dllimport/dllexport) if you strive for cross platform code, however you will need to add .DEF file to the project with all exported names. Alternatively, you can define a macro that will expand to __declspec(dllimport) for client builds, to __declspec(dllexport) for the DLL build and to nothing for Unix builds. 2. Change the project type to DLL instead of LIB. I think the easiest way is to create new DLL project with VC++ and add to it existing source files. This was the easy part. Then you will need to think out the types transferred between DLL and its callers. If these types require allocation/freeing memory, then both DLL and its client must use DLL version of CRT in order to preserve memory heap integrity. The other way is to export additional functions that will within DLL free whatever was allocated there. Or you can fall back to fundamental C types in the same way as Win32 API does, for example. 2009-Jul-17 14:07:21 by burnett: Potential Pitfall Microsoft Visual C++ compilers do not allow the linking controll that the GNU linker "ld" allows (i.e. --whole-archive, -no-whole-archive). All symbols need to be resolved by the VC++ compiler for both the loadable library and the application executable individually and thus it can cause duplication of libraries when the library is loaded. This is especially bad when using static variables (i.e. used in singleton patterns) as you will get two memory locations for the static variable, one used by the loadable library and the other used by the program executable. This breaks the whole static variable concept and the singleton pattern. Thus you can not use a static variable which is referenced by by both the loadable library and the application executable as they will be unique and different. To use a unique static variable, you must pass a pointer to that static variable to the other module so that each module (main executable and DLL library) can use the same instatiation. On MS/Windows you can use shared memory or a memory mapped file so that the main executable and DLL library can share a pointer to an address they both will use. From: http://www.yolinux.com/TUTORIALS/LibraryArchives-StaticAndDynamic.html 2009-Oct-21 15:36:33 by psilord: Ben Burnett has left the Condor Project. This ticket is being unassigned. 2010-Oct-20 15:59:08 by jfrey: Bulk change of target version from v070504 to v070505 using ./ticket-target-mover. 2011-Jan-27 14:21:33 by danb: Bulk change of target version from v070505 to v070506 using ./ticket-target-mover. 2011-Feb-01 14:49:30 by tannenba: Bulk change of target version from v070506 to NULL using ./ticket-target-mover.

title: Ticket #4736: Nordugrid jobs held when exit info missing
description: When a nordugrid job completes, the gridmanager queries the nordugrip ldap server to get the job's exit code and runtime information. If any of the information is missing, then it puts the job on hold. It turns out that most job information is optional, and what information is reported varies based on the local batch system. If the batch system is HTCondor, then nordugrid-job-usedwalltime isn't reported. It appears that nordugrid-job-usedcputime is already reported, with a default value of 0 if the underlying stats aren't collected from the batch system. We should change the gridmanager so that it throws an error only if no information is returned, and use reasonable defaults when individual values are missing. Also, when the gridmanager does throw an error, ensure a reasonable hold reason is set. Previously, we had the useless "Unspecified gridmanager error".

title: Ticket #4448: Improve performance of putClassAd with projection
description: the worker function putClassAd is very inefficient in the way it handles projections. A few minor changes will make this function a lot faster which in turn will reduce the CPU useage of the collector and the schedd when handling typical condor_status and condor_q requests. The changes are require that the projection be a list of attributes, not a list of expressions use classad::References (i.e. std::set) rather than StringList to hold the list of attributes. expand the list of attributes by looking only at internal references do the expansion of attributes inside the call to putClassAd These changes together seem to reduce the CPU cost of sending ads from the collector for a typical condor_status query by about half. the reduction in CPU cost to the schedd for handling condor_q requests should be similar, but no timing numbers are available yet.

title: Ticket #3677: StarterWaitForDebug / ShadowWaitForDebug easily abused
description: If a job ad contains StarterWaitForDebug=1 or ShadowWaitForDebug=1, the respective daemon will enter an infinite loop until the parent daemon gives up and kills it. The intent is to provide an opportunity to attach with a debugger, clear the value, and move on. However, this is an easy way to, at least briefly, denial of service a slot and to chew up a lot of CPU on a submit machine. The harm is relatively minor; a user can, naturally, just run jobs that are infinite loops, and eventually the parent daemon will deem the starter/shadow non-responsive and kill it. But it seems like we could do better. In particular, the daemon in question becomes unresponsive. This means that policy for the slot may be ignored for a while as the starter is unwilling to help. It's also possible to do this accidentally and end up tying up machines you can't fix yourself. Possible improvements: At least have the loops call sleep(0), so we don't chew up so much CPU. A knob to turn off the functionality that defaults to off? The ability to restrict which users can use the functionality?
creator: adesmet

title: Ticket #5609: Docker universe should advertise cpu usage
description: Currently, docker universe jobs report wall time, but not cpu (user or system) time. The procd can't measure these directly, as the actual job is rooted under the docker server, which is not a child of the starter. The docker stats API exposes job and cpu runtime, but not all the way to the CLI tools. So, to get the usage, HTCondor will need to either call the API directly, which we have not done for previous docker integration, or get the usage directory from the container's cgroup. We've been uneager to do the latter, because we'd like the cgroup that docker uses to be somewhat abstracted from HTCondor. Another issue is that the stats api doesn't report usage for containers that have been stopped or exited. This means that the starter will need to poll for usage, and will miss any usage that happens between the last polling period and job exit. The starter will poll these statistics more frequently than the job update interval in order to minimize such lossage. The api exposes both user and system cpu, which the starter will insert in the RemoteSysCpu and RemoteUserCpu, in seconds.

title: Ticket #5259: Shared port daemon leaks file descriptors.
description: The shared port audit log code has a file descriptor leak. This code is triggered when using an on-disk file (on Linux) to pass a socket from the shared port daemon to the target daemon. An on-disk file will be used (on Linux) if CONDOR_PRIVATE_SHARED_PORT_COOKIE is not set in the environment of the target daemon. This will only occur if USE_SHARED_PORT is false for the master, and will only matter if USE_SHARED_PORT is true for the target daemon. The glideInWMS factories (and possibly front-ends) use this configuration model, probably to avoid dealing with shared-port collector trees. The relevant config fragment is something like: USE_SHARED_PORT = FALSE DAEMON_LIST = $(DAEMON_LIST) SHARED_PORT SCHEDD.USE_SHARED_PORT = TRUE SHADOW.USE_SHADED_PORT = TRUE There is a work-around: starting the master with CONDOR_PRIVATE_SHARED_PORT_COOKIE set in the environment, as it will propogate down to the target daemon(s). Note that this should not be set in any world-readable file (including /etc/sysconfig/condor), because it would allow unauthorized processes to use the shared port daemon. Consider adjusting /etc/init.d/condor and setting that to be mode 0700 instead; or upgrade to 8.4.0 when it's available.

title: Ticket #6863: scitokens: can't do secure file read/write with non-root WSGI apps
description: The OAuth credmon webserver reads information from "keyfiles" that the condor_credd writes out at submit time if a user requests OAuth tokens that don't exist. Currently, the credd writes these files as (owned by) root using write_secure_file() with as_root = true . See line 343 in /src/condor_credd/credd.cpp . This is a problem if the webserver is running as non-root, which is likely if the admin is running the webserver as a WSGI app. For now, we should assume that it's running as the same effective user as condor. More thinking/code may be needed later for the case where an admin is running condor as root, but the webserver is running as a less privileged user. This ticket has expanded beyond reading/writing to the keyfile to the more general case of any time condor read/writes to files that are going to be read/written by a non-root process (e.g. the OAuth Credmon web application running as a WSGI app).
remarks: 2019-Jan-18 13:56:46 by jpatton: This needs some further discussion. as_root = true should not be a problem if the condor daemons are truly running under a different actual uid, but is a problem if the daemons are actually running as root but effectively as a different user (e.g. the same user as the WSGI application that reads the keyfile and writes tokens). Using as_root = true is also causing problems where read_secure_file() is being used in the credd and shadow. WSGI apps should not be started as root (though they can be given sudo privs). We should think about this carefully. 2019-Jan-18 16:06:15 by jpatton: After today's discussion, let's set some short-term and long-term fixes: Short term: Add a config option (CREDD_TRUST_FILES or something of TJ's liking) that would allow the credd and shadow (and starter?) to trust files in SEC_CREDENTIAL_DIRECTORY regardless of which uid owns the files or what the permissions of the files are set to. This will allow testers like Duncan to turn on this knob and allow the credmon and its related WSGI app to work without running as root. On the admin side, admins will need to set the GID sticky bit on the directory for SEC_CREDENTIAL_DIRECTORY and set group ownership to a group that includes both condor and apache (or whatever user the WSGI app is running as). Files should be written with at least u+r and g+r permissions. Long term: We need some way to give the credd and shadow confidence that token and key files are only readable and writable by root and a trusted user (the one running the WSGI application). We could check permissions to make sure they are not group or world readable, or we could be even more strict and check that the owner matches a uid given by the admin in the condor_config. This requires some more thinking, so we should create a new ticket to track progress for the longer term fix. 2019-Feb-06 13:54:11 by jfrey: Code Review Ideally, read_secure_file() would have an option to verify file permissions that allows the group read permission that write_secure_file() can set. But that's not needed for this ticket.

title: Ticket #690: dprintf initialization around fork() is broken
description: I ran into the dprintf_failure.MASTER problem with an EBADF on the lock fd again, this time in the V7_3_2-branch, as described in the remarks of #123. This problem is very hard to debug because it exists just at the boundary of a fork. Basically. the master forks a child, and the child thinks the LockFd is valid when in reality it is closed and when it tries to dprintf (in the param() system in this case) debug_lock() fails badly and writes the above file. Also the dprintf API calls to dprintf_wrapup_fork_child() and dprintf_init_fork_child() don't seem to be called at all, which is very disturbing. This is a showstopper because A) apparently it is easy to get the system into this state, and B) once it happens, who knows what incantation caused it or how to fix it. This needs fixing! I've been debugging it, but no luck so far. It remains elusive.

2009-Aug-24 21:38:06 by psilord: Ok, I think I finally found it! In daemon_core_main.cpp, around 1906, we see this block of code: if ( get_mySubSystem()->isType( SUBSYSTEM_TYPE_MASTER ) ) { int fd_null = safe_open_wrapper( NULL_FILE, O_RDWR ); if ( fd_null < 0 ) { fprintf( stderr, "Unable to open %s: %s
", NULL_FILE, strerror(errno) ); dprintf( D_ALWAYS, "Unable to open %s: %s
", NULL_FILE, strerror(errno) ); } int fd; for( fd=0; fd<=2; fd++ ) { close( fd ); if ( ( fd_null >= 0 ) && ( fd_null != fd ) && ( dup2( fd_null, fd ) < 0 ) ) { dprintf( D_ALWAYS, "Error dup2()ing %s -> %d: %s
", NULL_FILE, fd, strerror(errno) ); } } // Close the /dev/null descriptor _IF_ it's not stdin/out/err if ( fd_null > 2 ) { close( fd ); // line 1906!!!!! } } Given the flow of the code around line 1906, it would appear to me that the close(fd) in line 1906 should be close(fd_null) instead. Otherwise, fd is left at 3 due to the fd++ in the for loop. In my specific case, fd 3 happens to be the LockFD for the dprintf() system. 2009-Aug-24 21:59:36 by psilord: Fixed the errant close(fd) to be close(fd_null) in line 1906. It worked when I tested it, and I committed it to V7_3_2-branch and merged it to master. I consider this ticket resolved.

description: The SCHEDD should keep track of counts of idle/running/held/etc jobs overall and also by user and it should report those counts to condor_q and possibly to other places. title: Ticket #3698: Proper gsoap crashes
description: Fedora/EPEL adds a patch to their gsoap for IPv6 support. Unfortunately, this changes the layout of struct soap. By default, objects compiled against the EPEL /usr/include/stdsoap2.h result in code INCOMPATIBLE with /usr/lib64/libgsoapssl++.so. Things will link fine, but segfault at runtime. One variant of this issue is when a Globus callout is made where the globus plugin uses gsoap - half the symbols are from condor and half from the gsoap library. So, the plugin, condor, and the gsoap library all need to be compiled with '-DWITH_IPV6'. This affects PROPER builds only; UW builds were fixed in #3625 (in UW builds, we statically link in libgsoapssl++ and hide symbols from IPv6). The fix for #3625 also broke compilation on SL6 for HTCondor 8.0.0 when PROPER and gsoap are enabled (symbol visibility issues). To fix this, we need to compile anything that uses gsoap with '-DWITH_IPV6'. We should turn this on for PROPER builds but have the code continue to work even if the gsoap version used doesn't have the IPv6 patch.
remarks: 2013-Jun-12 15:00 by johnkn: Alan, please review Brian's patch, and if it looks ok, cherry-pick it back to the V8.0-branch. 2013-Jun-28 16:34:42 by adesmet: Review notes (Finished 2013-Jul-08) condor_sockaddr::condor_sockaddr(const sockaddr_storage * sa) 's implementation doesn't work. It looks like the intent is to call another constructor. What it actually does is construct a temporary condor_sockaddr and immediately discard it; the immediate object remains uninitialized. The code in condor_sockaddr(const sockaddr * saddr); needs to be moved to a shared function and both functions should call it. Actually it doesn't look like the new constructor is being used at all. But... likely to be useful in the future. RESOLVED: How safe is relying on sizeof(sockaddr_in) not matching sizeof(sockaddr_storage). Seems highly likely to work, but is it actually guaranteed? (Also, confirm that struct soap::peer is actually sockaddr_in) RESOLVED: In soap_core.cpp, why are we memcpying when simple assignment should work? Resolution: It doesn't work because we need to make the compiler happy, and it won't let us slip invalid code through just because it's on a code that that should never be run. Sadly, the preprocessor lacks knowledge of types and sizeof, so it can't help us. We could solve the problem with a compile time option, but that makes making a mistake easier. We could solve the problem with a mess of casting, but that's a mess of casting. Brian's solution appears to be the best one we're left with. if (sizeof(cursoap->peer) == sizeof(sockaddr_storage)) then presumably cursoap->peer is sockaddr_storage, and a straight assignment should work. else then (hopefully? ASSERT(sizeof(cursoap->peer) == sizeof(sockaddr_in))?), cursoap->peer is sockaddr_in, and simple assignment should work. Why is to_storage monkeying around with copying? Can't we just return this->storage? Ideally add unit tests for the new condor_sockaddr constructor and condor_sockaddr::to_storage to /src//condor_unit_tests/OTEST_condor_sockaddr.cpp . I'm most worried about the new constructor, as it's unused. Match local style. /src/condor_daemon_core.V6/soap_core.cpp cuddles braces next to if/else. (True in condor_sockaddr.cpp as well, but the code in question is going to disappear per point 4.) Would the name daemon.proper.version be better than daemon.version.proper? ".version" is arguably the extension ("This is a version script, suitable for passing to ld --version-script"). Seems like it would more obviously connect it to the existing daemon.version. RESOLVED: I was unclear about the purpose of the custom linker script; bbockelm's explaination below satisfies me. 2013-Jun-28 18:45:37 by bbockelm: Thoughts: Bah. I always screw up constructors in C++. Will fix. We are guaranteed that sizeof(sockaddr_in) != sizeof(sockaddr_storage) -- at least on platforms which have IPv6 support. The definition of sockaddr_storage is that it must be castable to sockaddr_in if it is an IPv4 address. "struct soap::peer" is of type sockaddr_storage if "-DWITH_IPV6" is handed to the compiler; otherwise, it is sockaddr_in. That headache is the whole reason for this patch... Simple assignment doesn't work. See below. I guess I could reinterpret_cast and do some pointer manipulation if you'd prefer that over memcpy. Didn't realize that condor_sockaddr is a union. I can switch to returning this->storage. /usr/include/sys/socket.h:359:8: note: candidate function (the implicit copy assignment operator) not viable: no known conversion from 'const sockaddr_in' to 'const sockaddr_storage' for 1st argument; Anything else? If you can respond to points 2 and 3, I will commit fixes to 1 and 4. 2013-Jul-01 11:06:16 by adesmet: Sorry, you caught my review halfway done. I'm keeping my work in progress in the ticket. Almost done. However, I believe we're in agreement on points 1-4. 2013-Jul-01 11:16:10 by adesmet: Upon re-consideration, I stand by point 3. I'd expect something like this: if (sizeof(cursoap->peer) == sizeof(sockaddr_storage)) { cursoap->peer = socket->peer_addr().to_storage(); } else { ASSERT(sizeof(cursoap->peer) == sizeof(sockaddr_in)); cursoap->peer = socket->peer_addr().to_sin(); } It's not clear from the error message you cite what the compiler doesn't like. As best I can tell, the types are the same, and the default assignment implementation should work fine. 2013-Jul-01 11:21:34 by adesmet: Doh! Bad Alan, no pretending that you can mix compile-time and run-time evaluation. So, yeah, Brian, you're correct on point 3. Seems like a better solution should exist, but mine isn't it. Thinking... 2013-Jul-01 11:27:39 by adesmet: Right, Brian's solution for point 3 is as good as I can think of. That's resolved. 2013-Jul-01 15:56:34 by johnkn: As per Brian's request, I cherry picked 092ec6af24571e2 into the V8_0-branch (for 8.0.1). For posterity, here was my response: Here's where things go awry. libgsoap++ does *not* include these functions. Rather, it expects these to be provided by executable linking against the library, as it has missing references to these. UW-build: These symbols all remain hidden as libgsoap++ is statically linked against the condor_* binary. No gsoap-related symbols are publicly exported. Thus, any plugin using gsoap can be loaded by condor without worrying about symbol leakage. PROPER-build: These symbols are public in order for the binary to be successfully linked against libgsoap++. Thus, any plugin using gsoap must use the exact same set of defines as HTCondor and the system compilation of libgsoap++ in order to use the same symbols (hence the addition of -DWITH_IPV6). gsoap is a bad, bad library in that the structures align differently depending on the defines - and the Fedora/EPEL packaging makes it so programs use the wrong set of flags by default. title: Ticket #940: Batch leases for cream jobs
description: With cream, leases are their own entities. The client creates a lease on the server with a unique name and an expiration date. The client can then associate that lease with any number of subsequent jobs. Lease renewal is done to the lease entity. When the lease expires, all jobs associated with it are removed. Currently, Condor creates a separate lease for each job. Most jobs could share the same lease. We have discovered that having a separate lease per job has huge performance issues when scaling up to thousands of jobs, on both the client and the server.

title: Ticket #413: dagman has linear search when parsing dag
description: So, I had performed a test to see if dagman could handle a one million node dag. The structure of the dag is one parent, 1 million children, then one end node. It turns out it took 2 hrs and 30 minutes to parse! This was because the parent/waiting/child structures for each node were linked lists. When a new node was added as a child to the original parent node, a linear search happened to determine if it had already been added. If not, it was added. So, this became an n^2 algorithm. I replaced the SimpleList structure with an STL set instead. This sped it up to 2 minutes and 30 seconds for the parse. However, it broke the DFSVisit code which was written before the Priority stuff went in. So, once I fix that latter, and write some tests, I'll check it in. Hopefully, it'll build everywhere since it uses the STL. :)

title: Ticket #4274: Excessive Negotiator lookups
description: I used the non-blocking condor_q protocol as a mechanism to find blocking activity in the schedd (in one terminal, do "strace condor_q 2>&1 | grep select" to look for blocking; in a second terminal, call pstack to see what the schedd is doing). One of the most common reasons for blocking was sending reschedule commands to the negotiator. On a busy node, this was called every 3-4 seconds and took about a second to resolve the sinful string of the negotiator (as this causes a blocking collector query). We should cache the daemon object corresponding to the negotiator (and hence sinful string) for a non-trivial amount of time.
remarks: 2015-Oct-27 15:09:35 by gthain: We used to only send the reschedule once every 20 seconds, but now with the timeslicing code, we only delay sending the reschedule command if the schedd is spending too much time negotiating. Seems to me that no matter how fast negotiation is, pushing the elevator button multiple times isn't a good use of the schedd's time.

title: Ticket #4126: queue argument to condor_submit should be expression
description: It would be handy if the number of jobs to queue on the "queue X" line in the submit file could be an expression calculated in the context of the job's ClassAd. With some ClassAd cleverness, you can have a single submit file vary options to the job. (See VaryArgumentsByProcId) To take a simple example: executable = myprogram.exe arguments = $$([names[ProcId]) +names = {"Alan", "Betty", "Claire"} queue 3 Ideally I'd be able to replace the last line with: queue size(names) When names is large, this would be much easier. And if you're permuting multiple lists of different lengths, you could automatically calculate the total number of jobs with something like: queue size(x)*size(y)*size(z)
creator: adesmet

title: Ticket #3749: Use filesystem namespaces to present non-changing execute directory
description: When USE_FS_NAMESPACES=TRUE, we should use filesystem namespaces to lie about the current working directory, presenting a constant, unchanging answer. Perhaps /work, or perhaps the $(Iwd) (the CWD when the job was submitted)? Rationale: some self-checkpointing software is ill behaved and encodes absolute paths in their checkpoints. When they move, they get cranky. Implementing this allows such software to Just Work. $(Iwd) seems optimal becaue the job's environment looks more like the submit point. If the job has hard coded paths to things in $(Iwd), it is more likely to Just Work. Concrete example: #3747: DMTCP checkpoints can't handle being moved
creator: adesmet

title: Ticket #1774: The ExitCode attribute is magic, appears to be mostly broken
description: I've got a 7.4.4 Linux scheduler and 7.0.5 execute nodes. I'm trying to form a on_exit_hold expression that holds jobs that don't exit with a 0 code. The ExitCode is not in the ad after a job completes, but testing if it's undefined returns false. For example: [root@anpvgrd1 log]# condor_q -l 24 | grep -i exit ExitStatus = 0 ExitBySignal = FALSE WhenToTransferOutput = "ON_EXIT" OnExitHold = isUndefined(ExitCode) != FALSE OnExitRemove = isUndefined(ExitCode) RequeueReason = "The job attribute OnExitRemove expression 'isUndefined(ExitCode)' evaluated to FALSE" I would have expected isUndefined(ExitCode) to return True because ExitCode is definitely not in the job's ad. It's un-printable: [root@anpvgrd1 log]# condor_q -f "%s\n" ExitCode [root@anpvgrd1 log]# Un-eval-able: [root@anpvgrd1 log]# condor_q -f "%s\n" 'ExitCode == 0' [root@anpvgrd1 log]# FWIW the following works when my scheduler is Windows and either 7.0.5 or 7.4.4: OnExitHold = (ExitCode != 0) OnExitRemove = (ExitCode == 0) In that case the jobs hold and remove properly according to their ExitCode values. This appears to be some Linux scheduler/Windows execute node anomaly.
creator: ichesal

title: Ticket #5672: auth code problems in 8.5.5
description: In OSG we did the 8.5.5 pre-release smoke test and ran into an issue, for details see: https://jira.opensciencegrid.org/browse/SOFTWARE-2327 The error was: SECMAN:2010:Received "DENIED" from server for user unauthenticated@unmapped using no authentication method, which may imply host-based security. Our address was '::1', and server's address was '::1'. Check your ALLOW settings and IP protocols. Can't send Reconfig command to local master Tim T said Zach would need to look. Tim can add more comments also as he might have a better idea about the problem.
remarks: 2016-May-12 16:24:15 by zmiller: Definitely smells like an IPv6 issues, so I am reassigning to Todd Miller. 2016-May-12 16:58:01 by edquist: COMMAND: condor_reconfig -debug EXIT STATUS: 1 STANDARD OUTPUT: 05/12/16 12:13:41 condor_read() failed: recv(fd=3) returned -1, errno = 104 Connection reset by peer, reading 5 bytes from <[::1]:9618>. 05/12/16 12:13:41 IO: Failed to read packet header 05/12/16 12:13:41 SECMAN: no classad from server, failing ERROR SECMAN:2007:Failed to end classad message. Can't send Reconfig command to local master STANDARD ERROR: [none] 2016-May-23 14:44:40 by edquist: Attaching logs & config from a successful 8.5.4 run... 2016-May-26 14:53:58 by tlmiller: So the biggest problem in the logs was that the shared port daemon wasn't working. Turning off SELinux (completely -- disabled rather than permissive-mode) resolved that issue. Experimentation revealed that starting HTCondor from the shell also avoided the problem, which suggests that systemd is Up To Something(TM). (I was also fiddling with turning off the HTCondor "socket" system service-thing, but in retrospect I'm not sure that was actually doing anything -- I think "stopping" the socket service-thing was actually a no-op.) However, even with the shared port daemon working, the authorization failure was still occurring. This isn't surprising, given that ::1 really wasn't in the authorized list. Since the client tools didn't use ::1 when HTCondor was started from the shell, I suspect the problem is how inheriting the socket from system means that HTCondor's command socket and configuration may disagree with each other. Additionally, systemd binds both IPv4 and IPv6 to the same listen socket. We distinctly chose not to do this in the HTCondor networking code, and may have odd problems a result. For instance, I'm guessing that the address of the command port made it into the address file, and ::1 is the best we could do with such a weird hybrid entity. See ticket #5690. This ticket is otherwise resolved by disabling socket activation in the packaging for systemd-enabled distributions.

Similarly, when you click on a row in a table, modifying the linked graph, no URL change. Both should update the URL in a way that allows bookmarking and going back and forward. This could be through manipulating the history directly, probably by manipulating the search arguments. There is some old commented out code in htcondorview.js for doing this. (index.html?foo=bar) The other option is manipulating document.location directly with anchors (index.html#foo=bar); that should allow the history to just work.
creator: adesmet

title: Ticket #5222: enable classad caching by default on Windows
description: classad caching was enabled by default in non-windows platforms last series. But on windows there was an occasional intermittent crash on shutdown that prevented this. A recent change to free more things on shutdown (part of the Valgrind work), made this crash on exit on Windows 100% reproducible. The problem is that the classad cache is essentially a static global class, and it can be destructed before all of the classads are destructed when the classad library is statically linked into a binary - which it is on windows. The fix is a bit hacky, but essentially, we add a flag at global scope that short-circuits calls to remove items from the cache after it has been destructed. This fixes the crash on exit, and allows us to make the configuration for classad caching the same on Windows as it is on other platforms.

title: Ticket #5808: Be able to pass result from one DAG node to another
description: Just got a request today on htcondor-users to be able to pass the result from one node to another node: JOB A foo.sub SCRIPT POST A bar.sh $RETURN JOB B bar.sub VARS B=$(RETURN) That syntax wouldn't quite work, but maybe something like this would: JOB A ... JOB B ... VARS B result="$RESULT(A)" SCRIPT PRE B my_script $RESULT(A) Of course, this only works if job A has finished before job B runs. I'm not sure if we should require that B is a "descendant" of A, or if it should just be a run-time error if we get to B and A hasn't finished... Also, if node A fails, and B is a descendant of A, B will never get run. So maybe this is only relevant if A has a POST script and we actually want the return value of A's HTCondor job, not node A as a whole.

title: Ticket #6377: split docker run into docker create + docker start
description: Currently, docker universe jobs are started with the "docker run" command, which does two things -- it creates the container, potentially fetching the image, and runs the job in the container. Newer versions of docker now support splitting these operations into their component parts -- a "docker create" command, which does the fetching and provisioning of the container, and a "docker start", which simply starts the command in the given container. This is like a fork + exec. Changing docker universe to use the latter pair gives us the opportunity to better detect and report errors, and to more accurate account for usage and status.

title: Ticket #3175: ClassAd caching leaks memory in Condor
description: Both CHTC and University of Nebraska have noticed massive memory leaks in Condor 7.9.0 daemons. After three weeks, the schedd on submit-1.chtc.wisc.edu was using 40GB of memory. In a personal Condor, the schedd leaks 1.2MB of memory after running 300 jobs. Disabling ClassAd caching via ENABLE_CLASSAD_CACHING causes the leaks to vanish. Valgrind shows that all of the leaked memory is allocated inside classad::CachedExprEnvelope. In most cases, the stack straces passes through MergeClassAds() and compat_classad::ClassAd::ChainCollapse(). I'll attach a full valgrind report.
remarks: 2012-Aug-06 13:36:49 by tstclair: So they stem from the code path where they ->Copy() prior to insert, but don't call the skip cache path because it's ref count is already updated. Also when looking up the references it seems like the interface is pretty leaky b/c imho we are doing far too much manipulation of the innerds of classads external to the actual interface. The most common examples that I see are searching through the adds looking for specific attribute names then copying then to some target ad. It makes far more sense to hide that under the interface. 2012-Aug-07 15:24:09 by jfrey: Isn't the problem in CachedExprEnvelope::cache(), in the EXPR_ENVELOPE case of the switch statement? That should be a direct assignment of pTree to pRet, rather than invoking Copy(). When ClassAd::Insert() is called, the ClassAd assumes responsibility for deleting the ExprTree pointer passed in. The caller shouldn't have to disable caching for the call. 2012-Aug-07 15:53:50 by jfrey: I just did a check with valgrind. Changing the pTree->Copy() to just pTree in CachedExprEnvelope::cache() fixes the memory leaks. That's without the changes you recently pushed. 2012-Aug-07 16:13:50 by tstclair: iirc that was in place to prevent a different issue which was arising. 2012-Aug-07 16:15:19 by tstclair: it's entirely possible that the issue is non-existent now. That mod would need to run through NMI, and I would need to revert the others.

remarks: 2013-Sep-03 15:19:56 by johnkn: -af foo behaves like -f "%v" foo. It gives the value of foo, which means that it gets evaluated if it is an expression. This is different from %s which does not evaluate. use -af 'unparse(foo)' to get un-evaluated values with autoformat. 2013-Sep-03 15:30:10 by pfc: *doh!* Thank you -- this makes perfect sense. PEBKAC. 2013-Sep-03 15:36:51 by johnkn: On further investigation. -f "%s" foo will evaluate foo and if the result is string-valued it will print the result, otherwise it unparses it. -long always prints raw (not-evaluated) classad attributes. But it seems like it might be useful to have a -af mode that always prints out un-evaluated attribute values like -long does.

title: Ticket #2271: CREAM user mapping incorrect in gridmanager
description: The key used for creating CreamResource objects in the gridmanager should match how a CREAM server maps users. title: Ticket #7073: Automatically set the alias for the collector
description: When we construct a generic daemon name from a hostname, we set an appropriate hostname alias in the sinful string for use in SSL and GSI peer certificate verification. This allows us to compare the hostname the user provided with the hostname(s) in the certificate. With this information, we no longer need to rely on reverse DNS (which is considered insecure) to go from the IP address in the sinful string to the hostname. Surprisingly, there are two sets of logic that generate a sinful from a hostname -- one is Daemon::getDaemonInfo and the other is Daemon::findCmDaemon. The alias is not set in the latter, resulting in issues verifying the hostname when someone does condor_status -pool foo.example.com and the collector at foo.example.com itself requires hostname verification. I'm marking this as a bug in 8.9.2 given that is the first release where SSL host verification is done by default.

title: Ticket #6398: schedd should retire noop_jobs when they are submitted.
description: The schedd currently only retires jobs that have IsNoopJob when it does count_jobs, which is does only about as often as it sends submitter ads to the collector. This means that a DAG that uses noop jobs as nodes will be often run slower than one that uses real, but trivial jobs that consume real execute resources. This is not ideal. Instead, we can set a transaction trigger on IsNoopJob and retire jobs where that evaluates to true right after the commit of the submit transaction, (or of the qedit if it is set post-submit). This will mean that count_jobs will only need to retire noop jobs that have an expression that becomes true only after the job has been alive for a while. see #6396 for the 8.6 bug that triggered this.

title: Ticket #3030: JobRouter should be able to route between multiple schedd's
description: For the Condor-CE, it would be very useful if the JobRouter could route between two schedd's on the same host. Having everything run in one schedd is difficult because: Writing a generic authz policy that merges the local authz and the remote authz is difficult to automate. Creating a merged condor_mapfile and GSI_AUTHZ_CONF may not be possible from a packaging standpoint. Detecting the location of the local site's configuration files so we can reliably "drop in" configs (as there are a huge number of variations of what sites have setup). The site may not want to expose their main collector / schedd to remote users to prevent against denial of service attacks. Dan has provided me with a draft patch that I've been using. remarks: 2014-Jan-23 12:39:25 by wenger: Created V8_0-gittrac_4171-branch for this. 2014-Jan-23 16:00:07 by wenger: Also see #3843. 2014-Jan-29 13:23:31 by wenger: The basic problem was this: condor_submit_dag needs to read the DAG file to find any per-DAG config files that are specified in the DAG file. Unfortunately, it was doing this by calling a MultiLogFiles method that read the entire file into a string in memory. DAGMan not using workflow log, job submit file does not define a log file -> events written to workflow/default log file without event mask. DAGMan using workflow log -> events written to workflow/default log file with event mask. (The three cases were implemented in the order they're listed.) Anyhow, as part of the fix to #4171, I made case # 2 the same as case # 3. I also did a few other cleanups: In the DAGMan job submission code, we only generate the event mask string once, instead of re-generating it for every submit (the string is the same every time anyhow). If we're in workflow log mode, we no longer look at Condor node job submit files at all, since we don't care if they specify a log file; previously we read the submit file even if we didn't care about the log file (#3843). title: Ticket #5275: Clarify documentation for DAGMan maxidle and maxjobs
description: Per multiple complaints from users (and Lauren, herself!), the documentation for "maxidle" and "maxjobs" features in the command-line manual pages is confusing. For example, the output for "man condor_submit_dag" says the following: -maxidle NumberOfJobs Sets the maximum number of idle jobs allowed before condor_dagman stops submitting more jobs. Once idle jobs start to run, condor_dagman will resume submitting jobs. NumberOfJobs is a posi- tive integer. If the option is omitted, the number of idle jobs is defined by configuration vari- able DAGMAN_MAX_JOBS_IDLE , which defaults to 1000. Note that for this argument, each individual process within a cluster counts as a job, which is inconsistent with -maxjobs . Nothing special is done to the submit description file. Setting queue 5000 in the submit description file, where -maxidle is set to 250 will result in a cluster of 5000 new jobs being submitted to the con- dor_schedd . In this case, condor_dagman will resume submitting jobs when the number of idle jobs falls below 250. Currently, the statement that "each individual process within a cluster counts as a job" is ambiguous, as it doesn't clearly specify that the count only applies to when DAGMan decides to submit the next "JOB" submit file (and that processes are not considered in a way that would only queue some of the processes for the next submit file). Lauren is happy to discuss this ambiguity further, and to show examples of users complaining about the confusion.

title: Ticket #5625: Overhaul grid universe job leases
description: The management of job leases in the grid universe needs several improvements. The calculation of leases is overly complex, especially when many jobs must share the same lease. Recently, users reported that the gridmanager was setting abnormally short leases for cream jobs, and it was difficult to trace the code to see how that could happen. There are also several inefficiencies in how leases are renewed for Condor-C jobs. We propose the following changes to the job lease code for the grid universe: All jobs managed by the same Resource object in the gridmanager share a single lease Lease duration is minimum of all current jobs Allow individual jobs to have no lease, where already supported (grid-type condor) Remove CalculateJobLease() function Simplify lease update sequence in BaseResource in the gridmanager Don't require synching of lease update in local job queue before doing update to remote server Remove ATTR_LAST_JOB_LEASE_RENEWAL_FAILED Update lease expiration time in local Job objects only after remote operation succeeds The following changes will be considered for a future release: In c-gahp, use SetAttribute() with NoAck flag to update lease expiration times Consider requiring leases for grid-type condor jobs Make default lease duration configurable, possibly per grid-type

title: Ticket #4937: Fix time zone handling in ClassAds
description: When parsing an absTime value that doesn't have a time zone offset, the ClassAd library calculates the start and end of DST in the local time zone incorrectly. The times of switching to/from DST are off by the local zone's offset from UTC. AbsTime values within that several-hour window will be converted to the wrong UTC time (off by an hour in either direction). In time zones that follow the US's DST rules, this bug can be observed by evaluating the following expression: absTime("2002-10-27T17:30:00")-absTime("2002-10-27T02:30:00") The result should be relTime("15:00:00") With the bug, the result is relTime("16:00:00")

title: Ticket #653: Detect operating system, distribution, and version
description: We would benefit from having code that detects the operating system, distribution, and version. The dependent tickets below require such functionality to exist. Random notes: Detection on Windows is probably just GetVersionEx. Detection on Linux probably involves grovelling around on disk, looking at things like /etc/redhat-release, /etc/SuSE-release, /etc/issue (unreliable, but maybe a good fallback), and more. Novel on detecting distribution, a longer list of distribution specific files Proposed development order: Create new subdirectory for this work. condor_osdetect, perhaps. Create simple command line program that reports the detected OS. At first it won't do anything useful. It should link in various Condor libraries, notably c++_util, since we will likely eventually need safe_open_wrapper and the like. Also set up the Imake/autoconf stuff. Create a new static library for the os detection code. At first it should always report that it's unable to detect anything. The command line program should link in the library and use it to not do anything useful yet. Start adding actual detection capabilities to the library. At this point the command line program should be useful on at least one platform. Write a new test that runs the command line program and confirms the output. Add new detection and matching tests until we have "a bunch" Modify the condor_master to link this library and pass the information on. At this point the system is useful to local administrators. Modify the condor_collector to collect the information from many master ads and pass it on in the global ad. At this point the system is useful to Condor developers. while(there_are_undetected_platforms()) { add_more_detection_routines(); }

title: Ticket #6459: Submit shouldn't spool executable multiple times for same cluster
description: When copy_to_spool is set to True in the submit file, condor_submit tries to send the executable file over the network to the schedd once for each job in the cluster, when it only needs to do so once for the whole cluster. In 8.6 (#6454), we changed the schedd to decline executable spooling RPCs if the executable has already been received. That removed most of the wasted effort, but submit's behavior still introduces an extra round trip over the network per job within a cluster. We should make submit more intelligent about this. One wrinkle in how we implement this is how to treat a job cluster where the individual jobs have different values for copy_to_spool. The spooled executable is used by all jobs in the cluster. You can't use a spooled copy for only some of the jobs. I see a few ways to handle this: The executable is spooled only if job proc 0 requests it. This is easier to code. This is also how late materialization has to work. The executable is spooled if any job in the cluster requests it. This maintains the behavior of previous versions. The submission is aborted and an error reported.
remarks: 2017-Oct-19 15:57:49 by jfrey: Commit [52615] had the wrong ticket number in its commit message. It belongs under this ticket. 2017-Dec-13 15:30:32 by jfrey: We decided to spool the executable only if proc 0 of the cluster sets copy_to_spool=true.

Since a spooled executable is shared across a job cluster, sending it once per job is unnecessary and wasteful. (By Jaime Frey )

title: Ticket #2363: move CCB server to its own daemon
description: Currently, the collector is the CCB server. An incident in CHTC resulted in CCB problems causing a denial of service problem for the whole collector (see #2360). Although this specific problem has been addressed, there is a concern that something like this could happen again. Why was CCB service originally put in the collector? simplicity: the collector already has a well-known port that everything in the pool must be able to connect to, so in a simple deployment, we can just make use of that possibility of optimizing things so that the security session used by the CCB connection is the same as the one used by daemons to advertise themselves, thus reducing authentication overhead. This is not currently implemented, because the CCB registration happens at DAEMON authorization level, whereas the publication happens at something more specific, such as ADVERTISE_SCHEDD. Question: should daemons discover the CCB server by querying the collector? Or should they have a hard-coded CCB address, as they currently do? If they discover the CCB server, how should they pick which CCB server(s) to use? A name or list of names? An expression matching the CCB daemon ads?
creator: danb

title: Ticket #72: Some schedd invocations never evaluate periodic expressions
description: If the schedd's initialization takes longer than PERIODIC_EXPR_INTERVAL, the Timeslice code for periodic expression evaluation will return a negative number for the delay until the first call. This is passed to Register_Timer(), which takes an unsigned int, resulting in the callout never occurring. This bug shows up in the test suite as the job_core_perremove_sched test occasionally failing.

title: Ticket #2699: QSUB emulation for Condor
description: Earlier this year I asked if there is a way to perform SGE-style submissions of dependent jobs with Condor (i.e. qsub -hold_jid ...) https://lists.cs.wisc.edu/archive/condor-users/2011-January/msg00161.shtml The conclusion of this thread was that there is no built-in tool, but it wouldn't be impossible to build something like this from the building blocks that Condor provides. So I sat down and tried to come up with something minimalistic that does the job for our specific use-case. I ended up with a shell script that behaves like qsub (to a certain extent) and prepares submit files for condor_submit. It supports single jobs (scripts and command lines), array jobs ($SGE_TASK_ID,...) and specification of job dependencies via -hold_jid (monitored via a simple sentinel job running in the local universe). I'm attaching the current version of the script to this email, in case someone wants to use it as a source of inspiration. Any potential future development can be followed here: http://anonscm.debian.org/gitweb/?p=pkg-exppsy/condor.git;a=blob_plain;f=debian/condor_qsub;hb=HEAD I'd be glad to get feedback and patches. Michael

Its purpose is to serve as an adaptor between Condor and software that has been written to interact with SGE. condor_run imitates a (blocking) call to a (local) command. condor_qsub imitates a (non-blocking) call to a job-submission command (and to qsub in particular). In any case, it does not support to complete qsub API and is therefore limited to a subset of all potentially interesting use cases. However, it is currently very useful for interfacing to two core tools for neuro-imaging research (Nipype and FSL). There respective Debian packages are configured to work out-of-the-box with Condor, by using condor_qsub as adaptor. 2012-Sep-26 15:25:22 by tstclair: Seems contrib worthy, but I don't know if I would put it in mainline, because it's focus seems special purposed. title: Ticket #3572: Daylight savings time causes master to restart on Windows
description: Whenever the computer changes the clocks for daylight savings time, the condor_master is fooled into believing that condor_master.exe has been updated and will restart condor on that machine. This is caused by a circa 2007 workaround for a supposed bug in windows that would incorrectly adjust UTF file times for daylight savings time. The windows bug no longer exists, so the workaround is now a bug. UPDATE: 3/11/2014. There is an additional problem that showed up when daylight savings time switched on 3/9/2014. If the master timestamp is before daylight savings time, when daylight savings time kicks in the c-runtime and Windows appear to disagree about whether daylight savings should be added to the timestamp or not. See the bug at http://goo.gl/rBQjie It seems likely that switching to the 2012 c-runtime will fix this, but it would be even safer to just fetch the master timestamp using pure windows API and never convert it to localtime at all.

See http://goo.gl/qdNKt9 And see the bug microsoft bug report at http://goo.gl/rBQjie Is the runtime shipped with HTCondor the redistributable Vs2008 runtime of the redistributable Vs2010 ?

title: Ticket #7862: Issues configuring a "local issuer" SciTokens credmon
description: In order for a SchedD to run jobs on execute machines that might be version 8.9.6 or earlier and also 8.9.7 or later (as seems to be the case with OSG-Connect submit nodes) we need to upgrade the SchedD binaries to 8.9.9 and update the following: Config SchedD version 8.9.9 or later # Job transform that: # 0) Only applies to Vanilla universe (5) jobs # 1) Adds the scitokens credentials # 2) Conditionally sets SendCredential based on execute version # (Note: This expression evaluates versionLT() on the SchedD, so the SchedD # must be version 8.9.9 or later, but the execute nodes do not matter.) # JOB_TRANSFORM_AddSciToken @=end [ Requirements = (JobUniverse == 5); Eval_Set_OAuthServicesNeeded = strcat( "scitokens ", OAuthServicesNeeded ?: ""); Set_ZZZ_ExecuteVersion = "\$\$([split(TARGET.CondorVersion)[1]])"; Set_ZZZ_SendCredentialStr = "\$\$([versionLT(split(TARGET.CondorVersion)[1], \"8.9.7\")])"; Set_SendCredential = ZZZ_SendCredentialStr == "true"; ] @end # Point both credential directories to same spot. # This directory should be owned by root:condor and chmod 2770 SEC_CREDENTIAL_DIRECTORY_OAUTH = /var/lib/condor/oauth_credentials SEC_CREDENTIAL_DIRECTORY_KRB = $(SEC_CREDENTIAL_DIRECTORY_OAUTH) # Flag to new code to operate in local issuer mode LOCAL_CREDMON_PROVIDER_NAME = scitokens # For some reason, 8.9.9 has the SciTokens credmon in $(BIN) and not $(SBIN) CREDMON_OAUTH = $(BIN)/condor_credmon_oauth # This is where the python credmon is putting the log and it won't start if this isn't defined: SEC_CREDENTIAL_MONITOR_OAUTH_LOG = $(LOG)/CredMonOAuthLog OLD -- Workaround for 8.9.8 -- SUGGEST UPGRADE TO 8.9.9 INSTEAD Edit condor config: # Point both credential directories to same spot. # This directory should be owned by root:condor and chmod 2770 SEC_CREDENTIAL_DIRECTORY_KRB = $(SEC_CREDENTIAL_DIRECTORY_OAUTH) # Flag to new credmon code to look for krb-style filename but still generate oauth-style token. LOCAL_CREDMON_KRB_MODE = TRUE # *DO* define the sec credential producer SEC_CREDENTIAL_PRODUCER = /usr/bin/scitokens_credential_producer Edit credmon library files: In /usr/lib/python2.7/site-packages/credmon/CredentialMonitors modify LocalCredmon.py and OAuthCredmon.py as so: (This patch file is also at the bottom of the ticket as an attachment, scitokens.patch) --- a/LocalCredmon.py +++ b/LocalCredmon.py @@ -1,5 +1,6 @@ import os +import shutil import glob import scitokens @@ -75,13 +76,20 @@ class LocalCredmon(OAuthCredmon): <cred_dir> / <username> / <provider>.top """ # Take the cred_dir out of the cred_path - base, _ = os.path.split(cred_fname) + if htcondor.param.get("LOCAL_CREDMON_KRB_MODE", False): + base = os.path.splitext(cred_fname)[0] + if not os.path.isdir(base): + os.makedirs(base, mode=0o2755) + else: + base, _ = os.path.split(cred_fname) username = os.path.basename(base) - if self.should_renew(base, username): + if self.should_renew(username, self.provider): self.log.info('Found %s, acquiring SciToken and .use file', cred_fname) success = self.refresh_access_token(username, self.provider) if success: + if htcondor.param.get("LOCAL_CREDMON_KRB_MODE", False): + shutil.copy(os.path.join(base, self.provider + '.use'), base + '.cc') self.log.info("Successfully renewed SciToken for user: %s", username) else: self.log.error("Failed to renew SciToken for user: %s", username) @@ -96,6 +104,9 @@ class LocalCredmon(OAuthCredmon): """ provider_glob = os.path.join(self.cred_dir, "*", "{}.top".format(self.provider)) + if htcondor.param.get("LOCAL_CREDMON_KRB_MODE", False): + provider_glob = os.path.join(self.cred_dir, "*.cred") + self.log.info("Looking for *.cred files since LOCAL_CREDMON_KRB_MODE is set, found {} files".format(len(glob.glob(provider_glob)))) for file_name in glob.glob(provider_glob): self.process_cred_file(file_name) --- a/OAuthCredmon.py +++ b/OAuthCredmon.py @@ -55,11 +55,13 @@ class OAuthCredmon(AbstractCredentialMonitor): if 'use_refresh_token' in token_metadata: if token_metadata['use_refresh_token'] == False: return False + lifetime_fraction = api_endpoints.token_lifetime_fraction(token_metadata['token_url']) + else: + lifetime_fraction = 0.5 # compute token refresh time create_time = os.path.getctime(access_token_path) - refresh_time = create_time + (float(access_token['expires_in']) * - api_endpoints.token_lifetime_fraction(token_metadata['token_url'])) + refresh_time = create_time + (float(access_token['expires_in']) * lifetime_fraction) # check if token is past its refresh time if time.time() > refresh_time: Now, condor_submit will generate a {username}.cred file in /var/lib/condor/oauth_credentials and the credmon is signaled to create /var/lib/condor/oauth_credentials/{username}/scitokens.use Description of problem and possible solutions The way that Derek at OSG was using their SciTokens credmon doesn't seem to be supported any longer since 8.9.7 due to changes in the credential management framework. Previously, submit would invoke the SEC_CREDENTIAL_PRODUCER, which would produce a dummy cred file that got written as scitokens.top in the SEC_CREDENTIAL_DIRECTORY. This is more like "Kerberos mode" in that it is just passing a credential directly, as opposed to "OAuth mode" which prompts the user to obtain credentials via web. However, in modern versions, we have split the credential directory into one SEC_CREDENTIAL_DIRECTORY_KRB and SEC_CREDENTIAL_DIRECTORY_OAUTH. Using the SEC_CREDENTIAL_PRODUCER triggers a "kerberos mode" store cred, which goes in the KRB directory which would be managed by a krb credmon. However, the OAuth credmon does not monitor that directory and is not looking for files name for that directory's convention (<username>.top for krb, as opposed to <username>/scitokens.top for the oauth directory). The currently shipping oauth credmon is meant to monitor the OAUTH cred directory, and also has a split personality: one part is for "local issuer" and is hard-coded to look for "scitokens.top" and the other is for normal oauth processing and looks for general <service>.top filenames with their associated .meta files. All this combined means that there is no mechanism for a job wanting "locally issued" tokens to just create a "scitokens.top" file in the OAuth directory and have the OAuth credmon create a signed token for that user as that was basically relying on hacky behavior when HTCondor only supported one mode or the other, and that behavior is different now that we support both. We need to have a config knob that says something like "scitokens_LOCAL_ISSUER = true" so htcondor knows to handle that type of oauth request differently. It's also not clear that having essentially two oauth credmons (local and normal) monitoring the same directory is a good idea unless they can figure out how not to step on each other. It seems like if they are going to operate on two different subsets of files, or different directories, and behave in different ways, then maybe their codebase should be split and they should be two separate daemons. (Further discussion on solutions is in the Remarks below and will be summarized here once a consensus is reached.)
remarks: 2020-Sep-22 15:48:31 by jpatton: Some thoughts: The LocalCredmon is not quite hard-coded to look for {cred_dir}/{username}/scitokens.top, though that is the default it fallsback to. It actually first looks at the condor_config for LOCAL_CREDMON_PROVIDER_NAME and looks for {cred_dir}/{username}/$(LOCAL_CREDMON_PROVIDER_NAME).top. The LocalCredmon {cred_dir} currently inherits its value from the OAuthCredmon which will get its value from SEC_CREDENTIAL_DIRECTORY_OAUTH (via utils.get_cred_dir()). Changing the LocalCredmon to look in SEC_CREDENTIAL_DIRECTORY_KRB would require a little bit of refactoring, but not an unfathomable amount. The way the LocalCredmon works to generate a $(LOCAL_CREDMON_PROVIDER_NAME).use token file is if it finds the .top file (contents do not matter) or finds that the .use token is about to expire, it uses LOCAL_CREDMON_PRIVATE_KEY and LOCAL_CREDMON_KEY_ID (default: "local") from the condor_config to generate a new .use file via a scitokens.SciToken object. My two cents: Without knowing how the credd side of things works exactly, I think the easiest solution is having condor_submit invoke some kind of "producer" to always create $(SEC_CREDENTIAL_DIRECTORY_OAUTH)/{username}/$(LOCAL_CREDMON_PROVIDER_NAME).top if LOCAL_CREDMON_PROVIDER_NAME is defined in the condor_config and if the .top file doesn't already exist, along with sending the $(CREDMON_OAUTH) a SIGHUP on submit to make sure the .use file is generated. 2020-Sep-23 07:13:23 by bbockelm: This really was designed to use the "kerberos mode". It doesn't seem very well suited to use the OAuth mode. I mean, we can make the OAuth mode act like Kerberos mode - but is that really the right way to go? 2020-Sep-23 07:50:14 by zmiller: I really think we do want to make it work in OAuth mode. It is an OAuth ticket a JWT It is managed by the same daemon that watches the OAuth directory Kerberos mode stores things in "username.top" format in a flat directory. As such, in Kerberos mode you can only store one credential Which also means people using this mode of SciTokens can never use Kerberos (maybe not a big deal) The wire mechanics for retriving an OAuth and Kerberos cred are different How they are inserted into the job (filename and env variable) are different If you want to query your cred users should run "condor_store_cred query-oauth" and not "condor_store_cred query-krb" It's a choice between making OAuth behave like Kerberos, or to make Kerberos behave like OAuth and although either could be done I think for the above reasons I would rather do the former. 2020-Sep-23 08:19:21 by bbockelm: There's no such thing as an "OAuth ticket". OAuth is framework for acquiring and moving opaque tokens to an entity. Accordingly, the local issuer scitokens-credmon most certainly doesn't do OAuth. With respect to wire changes -- right now, all the OSG pilots are configured to do OAuth-mode and all the schedds are configured to do Kerberos-mode. description: Add support for interactive jobs via a -interactive option to condor_submit, which effectively submits a short sleep job followed by an ssh_to_job -auto-retry -X -remove-on-interrupt. title: Ticket #7474: daemons other than the condor_master should not default to background
description: Daemons other than the condor_master should not fork themselves into the background unless they are passed the -b flag. Currently all HTCondor daemons assume background mode unless they are passed the -f flag, but this behavior only makes sense for the condor_master. Daemon-core should be changed so that it defaults to foreground mode in the absence of any flag, and it should have a function that a dameon can call at the top of main that changes the default to background. Only the condor_master will call this function. The motivating reason for this change is that it allows for a configuration only way to valgrind or strace a daemon. With the current code, the automatic inclusion of -f before <daemon>_ARGS makes a wrapper script necessary to valgrind or strace a daemon, but if we no longer automatically pass -f to child daemons, a wrapper script will no longer be necessary.
